rows.title: Animator/Motion Designer
rows.descriptionText:
Strategic Agenda is looking for a talented Animator & Motion Designer to join our creative team.
We work with UN agencies, NGOs, foundations and other organisations tackling some of the world’s biggest challenges. Our work spans film, animation, design, campaigns and digital content, often across multiple countries and languages.
We’re looking for someone who can do more than simply animate.
You’ll need to be highly proficient in Adobe After Effects, confident with video editing, and have practical 3D skills in Blender or Cinema 4D. Just as importantly, you’ll need either a design background or a very strong design sensibility.
You should understand typography, composition, colour, hierarchy and visual storytelling, and be able to take a concept, storyboard or set of style frames and turn it into something beautifully crafted and engaging.
What you’ll be doingCreating 2D and 3D animation and motion graphics for films, explainers, social content and campaigns.Animating typography, illustrations, icons, infographics and visual identities.Working primarily in Adobe After Effects, alongside Blender or Cinema 4D where appropriate.Developing animation from storyboards, style frames and existing design systems.Creating and integrating 3D elements into motion design and film projects.Contributing ideas to visual concepts and creative treatments.Editing video in DaVinci Resolve and/or Adobe Premiere Pro.Combining live-action footage, animation, 3D, graphics, sound and subtitles into finished films.Adapting content for different platforms, formats and aspect ratios.Working closely with designers, filmmakers, producers and project managers.Taking projects from initial creative development through to final delivery.
What we’re looking forStrong Adobe After Effects skills.Practical, professional-level skills in Blender or Cinema 4D.A strong design background or demonstrably excellent design sense.A very good understanding of typography, layout, composition, colour and visual hierarchy.Strong motion graphics and animation skills.Good working knowledge of Illustrator and Photoshop.Competence in DaVinci Resolve and/or Premiere Pro.The ability to work confidently across both 2D and 3D workflows.Good visual storytelling instincts.Strong attention to detail.The ability to take creative direction while also bringing your own ideas.Someone collaborative, curious and keen to develop.
Additional skills we’d value3D modelling, lighting, texturing and rendering.Character animation or rigging.Compositing animation and 3D elements with live-action footage.Colour grading in DaVinci Resolve.Basic sound design or audio editing.Experience working in an agency, production company or design studio.Experience creating content for international or multilingual audiences.
Who this would suitThis role would suit a strong junior or midweight animator / motion designer, probably with around 1–5 years’ professional experience, although we care much more about the quality of your work than the number of years on your CV.
We’re particularly interested in people who understand that good motion design starts with good design.
You might come from a graphic design, motion design, animation or filmmaking background. What matters is that you have strong visual judgement, solid 2D and 3D skills, and can make thoughtful creative decisions rather than simply execute instructions.
A strong showreel and portfolio are essential.
Why Strategic AgendaYou’ll work on a wide range of international projects, from short social animations and explainers to documentary films, campaigns and longer-form storytelling.
It’s a small, collaborative creative team, so you’ll have the opportunity to contribute ideas, work across disciplines and take increasing ownership of projects as you develop.

rows.title: Data Centre Infrastructure Intern
rows.descriptionText:
Launch your infrastructure career through a hands on 3 month opportunity supporting a senior technology leader on a live data centre deployment project.
This is an exciting opportunity for a recent graduate to gain direct, practical experience in physical infrastructure, data centre systems and compute deployment. Based in London, the role offers a three-month internship with a view to becoming a permanent position for the right candidate.
Company OverviewThis London-based technology startup is working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, data and physical computing infrastructure. The business is building technology designed to address complex challenges within the rapidly developing AI sector, providing an environment where graduates can gain exposure to both technical problem-solving and real-world infrastructure deployment.
Job OverviewAs a Data Centre Infrastructure intern, you will work closely with a highly experienced technology leader with more than 25 years of industry experience. Your focus will be supporting the deployment of core data centre infrastructure and helping bring compute capacity online.This is a practical support role suited to someone who enjoys solving problems, learning quickly and taking ownership of tasks. You will work directly under the guidance of the senior technology leader, responding to priorities and contributing across hardware, software and data centre systems.
Here's what you'll be doing:Support the deployment and commissioning of core data centre and compute infrastructure.Work directly with a senior technology leader to complete technical tasks and resolve operational problems.Assist with troubleshooting across hardware, software, networking and physical infrastructure.Follow technical instructions carefully while developing your own judgement and problem-solving approach.Help bring compute capacity online and ensure deployment tasks are completed accurately and to a high standard.Communicate progress, issues and technical findings clearly throughout the deployment project.
Here are the skills you'll need:A relevant degree, ideally in Network Engineering or a closely related technical discipline.A genuine interest in physical infrastructure, data centres, networking and compute systems.Strong attention to detail and a willingness to complete work thoroughly without taking shortcuts.Clear communication skills, reliability and the ability to work closely with an experienced technical leader.A practical, hands-on approach to solving problems across software, hardware and infrastructure.The motivation to work in a fast-paced environment and take responsibility for completing tasks under direction.
Key perks and benefits:£24,000-£30,000 salary equivalent, Depending on prior experience.Three-month internship with a potential pathway to a permanent position.Direct exposure to a senior technology leader with extensive industry experience.Hands-on experience with live data centre and compute infrastructure deployment.Opportunity to develop practical technical, troubleshooting and problem solving skills.
Work PermissionsYou must have the right to work in the United Kingdom. Visa sponsorship is not available at this time.
Application ProcessThe hiring process is designed to move quickly and will involve a two-stage interview process, including an in-person interview in London. Candidates should be prepared to demonstrate their technical understanding, communication skills and enthusiasm for working hands-on with physical infrastructure.
Why Build Your Career in Data Centre Infrastructure?Data centre infrastructure provides graduates with a strong foundation across networking, hardware, compute and systems operations. As demand for computing capacity continues to grow alongside AI and other technology applications, practical infrastructure skills can provide opportunities to progress into specialist engineering, infrastructure operations and technical leadership careers.

rows.title: Data & Insights Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
What we do:Zero100 is a membership-based intelligence company that connects, informs, and inspires the world's most influential C-Level Operations & Supply Chain Officers - and their teams - to unlock the true potential of the AI and Digital Revolution. Our members use Zero100's our research, advisory services, data, and peer community, to sharpen strategy, challenge assumptions, and accelerate progress on their most important transformation priorities from AI adoption and digitization to resilience and decarbonization. With a rapidly expanding headquarters in central London, Zero100's members include Nike, Walmart, Unilever, Pfizer, Google, Honeywell, and General Motors.

Recent recognition: 2026 King's Award for Enterprise in the International TradeThe Sunday Times Best Places to Work 2025 The Sunday Times 100 (#43), 2025 LinkedIn Top 25 Start-Ups (#12), 2025 What you will do:Note that this is a primarily office-based role (~4 days per week).We are hiring a London-based Data & Insights Analyst to help deliver high-quality, evidence-based analysis that helps the world's top operations and supply chain leaders make better decisions. Your work will feed directly into the research, presentations, and advisory services we deliver to our members. You'll help translate complex datasets into clear, decision-oriented narratives for C-suite audiences, working closely with senior team members who will guide scoping and stakeholder framing as you build that muscle.In this role, you will run several distinct analyses a month, each for a different stakeholder and a different question. This is a high-output analytical role, not a long-cycle project role. The ability to get to a defensible data-based answer quickly, and to know when an answer is good enough, matters more than depth on any single piece of work.We're looking for someone with strong analytical fundamentals who has developed practical working habits with AI tools. You should know what good analysis looks like well enough to recognize when AI-generated output is useful, when it needs refinement or validation, and when it shouldn't be relied upon. We're looking for someone who sees these tools as part of a rigorous analytical workflow, not a substitute for structured thinking, sound judgment, or domain understanding. The strongest people we have hired all experiment with AI tools in their own time. We are less interested in courses or certifications and more interested in what you have actually made.The right candidate has experience translating data into insights for senior stakeholders, not just building dashboards. A comfort with ambiguity, structured thinking, willingness to work across diverse problem spaces, and strong communication skills is important. This role is not customer-facing out of the gate, but as you grow, there will be increasing opportunity to shape what we investigate, bring forward original insights, and eventually engage directly with customers.Beyond the day job, we are looking for candidates who share our enthusiasm about the potential for Zero100 to have a positive impact on the supply chain profession and (more broadly) the planet.
Responsibilities: Answer specific business questions posed by customers, the Research team, and senior analysts (open-ended or loosely scoped requests), turning them into structured analysis that ends in a clear finding and a recommendation.Help transform complex datasets into clear, insight-driven narratives, with guidance from senior team members on tailoring for executive audiences.Support scoping of data needs for new analyses, partnering with data engineering on pipeline work and taking ownership of transformation, analysis, and visualization tasks within a defined scope.Maintain a high bar for accuracy and clarity in the insights you deliver.Work across structured and unstructured sources (survey data, executive interview transcripts, operational datasets, and qualitative research notes) to support insights that wouldn't surface from any single source alone.Leverage AI tools (including our internal LLM) to accelerate analysis and explore data, with an eye toward validating and refining output rather than taking it at face value.Collaborate closely with research, design, and customer-facing teams to understand stakeholder needs and deliver reliable, high-quality work.As you develop in the role, begin identifying opportunities to surface new insights and propose new lines of inquiry, building toward greater ownership of the analytical narrative.

Requirements

Requirements:2-4 years of experience in data analysis, insights, or a related field, with some demonstrated ability (or strong potential) to translate data into narratives for senior audiences.Note: if the majority of your last two years has been spent building or maintaining dashboards, pipelines, or reporting infrastructure, this is not the right role for you.Strong analytical fundamentals: SQL required, Python a plus; willingness to work in environments like Databricks.Experience producing data visualizations and charts (Excel/PowerPoint, or directly from analytical tools) that make an argument, we care about what a chart proves, not how it looks. Storytelling is a plus.Working familiarity with AI-assisted analysis and workflow tools, with a genuine curiosity about where they help and where they fall short. You use AI tools daily in your own analytical work and can describe specific instances where they changed how you approached a problem, evidence of building things with AI outside of work is a strong positive.Structured thinking and a growing comfort with ambiguity. You can take a well-scoped business question, determine what information matters, and translate complex or incomplete inputs into a clear point of view, with support from senior colleagues on more ambiguous problems.Strong collaboration skills. You work well embedded within a research team and can navigate a matrixed, geographically distributed organization.Excellent written and verbal communication skills - you can present data and findings in a way that would resonate with a senior or executive audience, even if you haven't done so independently yet.Familiarity with operations or supply chain is a plus, but curiosity and fast learning matter more.

Benefits

Competitive salary and bonus schemeUnlimited holidaysPrivate healthcare & Life InsuranceEnhanced pensionEnhanced Parental Leave PolicyCustom designed offices in central London with free breakfasts & snacks

rows.title: Environmental Data Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Job Description

Environmental Data Analyst

About Us

Tradeweb is a global leader in electronic trading across asset classes. As financial markets become increasingly interconnected, our technology enables efficient, multi-asset trading on a global scale. We serve more than 3,000 clients in more than 85 countries, including many of the world’s largest banks, asset managers, hedge funds, insurers, corporations, and wealth managers.

Creative collaboration and sharp client focus have helped fuel our organic growth. We facilitated average daily trading volume (ADV) of more than $2.8 trillion over the past four fiscal quarters, topping $3.3 trillion in ADV for the first quarter of 2026.

Since our IPO in 2019, Tradeweb has completed four acquisitions and doubled our revenues – and 2025 was our 26th consecutive year of record revenues.

The Opportunity

We are recruiting an Environmental Data Analyst to support the preparation, maintenance and assurance of our greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory. This is a data-driven role: the organisation reports emissions across multiple cycles each year, to more than one set of stakeholders and under more than one assurance process, and the analyst keeps that data accurate, traceable and on time.

The role centers on four areas: data collection and validation across GHG inventory books; book maintenance, estimation and reconciliation; assurance evidence preparation; and controlled automation of repetitive analyses. The analyst independently executes clearly defined workstreams, while the inventory owner retains responsibility for methodology, quality control and final sign-off.

What You’ll Do

 Data collection and validation – run the multi-cycle collection process across GHG inventory, covering several hundred data points; validate figures, investigate prior-year and variance discrepancies, and keep internal data providers internal teams engaged and responsive.  Book maintenance, estimation and reconciliation – maintain the GHG inventory and the supporting carbon accounting systems; assist in producing interim full-year estimates from part-year data, reconcile to actuals, document variances and maintain version control so the correct figures reach the correct audience.  Assurance evidence preparation – prepare evidence and documentation for multiple external assurance processes, support walkthroughs, respond to queries and keep the full inventory and methodology documentation at an assurance-ready standard year-round.  Controlled automation – build and maintain tooling that automates repetitive analyses such as business travel, office attendance and ledger clean-up, and improve datasets, dashboards and reporting processes to strengthen data quality. 

About You

 Prior relevant experience in data analysis, sustainability reporting, environmental data or a related area.  Advanced proficiency in Excel, with experience managing, analysing and reconciling large datasets.  A strong data orientation – comfortable working with large datasets, spotting anomalies building repeatable, well-controlled processes.  Working knowledge of the GHG Protocol (basic or university-level is sufficient) and a interest or experience in sustainability reporting.  Confidence using technology and AI to automate repeatable work and build reliable tooling around routine analyses.  Strong attention to detail, initiative and reliability: able to take a task from instruction through to completion in a deadline-driven cycle, escalating issues where necessary.  A self-starter who is organised and capable of working independently while collaborating with global stakeholders. 

Why join Tradeweb?

Your work will help Tradeweb understand its environmental footprint and give stakeholders confidence in the information we report. You’ll have the opportunity to make lasting improvements to how we manage emissions data across our global business, tackling complex data challenges and seeing the difference your work makes to our environmental reporting.

At Tradeweb, our values guide how we work: we share ideas, stay curious, take ownership, exceed expectations, act responsibly and embrace differences. Together, they create a collaborative and inclusive environment where everyone can contribute and succeed.

Benefits

We offer a comprehensive range of benefits designed to support our employees at every stage of life and career. These include enhanced parental leave, family-building and postpartum support through Maven, subsidised gym membership and a wide range of learning and development opportunities.

Specific offerings vary by location, and our team can provide further information about the benefits available to you during the recruitment process.

Additional Information

Business area: Sustainability

Role level: Associate

Contract term: Permanent

Location: London – hybrid working, with 1-2 days per week on-site

Applications: Open to internal and external applicants

Application closing date: The advert closing date is Thursday 8th October 2026 at 23:55; however, the role may close earlier if sufficient applications are received. We encourage candidates to apply as early as possible.

Interview process: Our interview process consists of two stages, designed to explore your relevant experience, analytical skills and technical knowledge. We’ll share further details about each stage with you as you progress through the process.

rows.title: Principal Data Scientist, Experimentation
rows.descriptionText:
About Tripadvisor

The Tripadvisor Group connects people to experiences worth sharing, and aims to be the world’s most trusted source for travel and experiences. We leverage our brands, technology, and capabilities to connect our global audience with partners through rich content, travel guidance, and two-sided marketplaces for experiences, accommodations, restaurants, and other travel categories. The subsidiaries of Tripadvisor, Inc. (Nasdaq: TRIP), include a portfolio of travel brands and businesses, including Tripadvisor, Viator, and TheFork.

At Tripadvisor experiences, the only thing we love more than travel is data. We slice it, we dice it, and we use it to empower our decision making.

What You Will Do

As a Principal Data Scientist you will be a leading individual contributor responsible for how experimentation works across the organisation.

You will lead through technical depth, setting the standards others work to and raising the quality of measurement and decision-making across the function.

You will build the capability that lets teams experiment well without central support: the standards, tooling and protocols that make good practice the default, and a strategy for how it develops over time.

Both the speed and the reliability of decision-making should improve as a result. You will also take on the measurement questions we cannot currently answer well, where traffic is thin or the outcomes that matter take months to appear.

You Will

Set the technical standard for experimentation across Product Data Science, from conventional A/B testing to quasi-experimental and Bayesian methods, and make it practical through protocols, frameworks and tooling.Partner with Product, Engineering and Data Platform teams to improve experimentation velocity without sacrificing rigour.Critically assess how experimentation and the decisions that follow it affect platform health and growth, and make that relationship visible to leadership.Own the measurement approach for Viator's most complex questions, where standard experimentation is insufficient and the method has to be designed rather than selected.Develop and validate the statistical methods the organisation relies on, including simulation-based verification that they behave correctly before teams depend on them.Act as the final technical authority on measurement validity, adjudicating disputed results and determining what the evidence does and does not support.Standardise recurring analytical and experimentation processes across the function, using automation and AI capabilities where they materially improve consistency, throughput or quality.Design and land methodological improvements with organisation-wide impact, such as variance reduction for difficult metrics, approaches for low-traffic surfaces, proxy and surrogate metrics for long-horizon outcomes, and designs that hold up where users compete for shared supply.Grow the technical depth of the wider team by reviewing designs, mentoring senior data scientists, and improving how people reason about measurement.Advise on where experimentation is the wrong tool and define what should be done instead.

Skills & Experience

Experience: Extensive experience in data science or a similar quantitative role, with a proven track record of supporting and influencing a product organisation.Statistical & Experimentation Expertise: Authoritative command of experimentation in all its forms, from experimental design and variance reduction to causal inference, bandits and Bayesian methods. You should be able to develop and validate methodology, not only apply it.Technical & Modelling Expertise: Expert level proficiency in Python and SQL. Deep, hands-on experience with statistical modelling, (quasi) experimentation, multi-arm bandits, and a wide range of machine learning techniques such as regression, classification and clustering.Product Acumen: Demonstrated ability to define, implement and operationalise crucial product and feature-level metrics from scratch.Partnership & Enablement: Demonstrated ability to improve how other teams work by providing guidance, tooling and protocols, increasing both the speed and the quality of their experimentation rather than absorbing the work yourself.Decision Impact & Platform Health: Ability to critically assess how product decisions affect platform health and growth over time, and to bring that perspective into how experiments are designed and interpreted.Standardising at Scale: Experience standardising processes, frameworks or methods across multiple teams, including the use of AI and automation to make good practice the default.Cross-Functional Partnership: Proven ability to build strong relationships and drive outcomes across Product, Engineering, Data Platform and other central functions, often without direct authority.Critical Thinking: Leader in critical thinking, with a demonstrated habit of establishing whether a result is trustworthy before establishing what it means.Communication: Exceptional ability to explain measurement, method and uncertainty clearly to technical and non-technical audiences at every level.Education: Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Data Science, Engineering, Physics, Economics, or a related quantitative field.

You could be an especially great fit if you have:

Experience with experimentation in a two-sided marketplace, where interference between users and finite shared supply complicate measurement.Experience building and validating proxy or surrogate metrics for long-horizon outcomes, and a clear view of how far they can be trusted.Experience with Bayesian and hierarchical approaches, particularly for low-traffic surfaces or pooling evidence across many small markets.Experience building or materially improving experimentation platforms, measurement frameworks, self-service capabilities or data products.Experience in a high-scale technology company, marketplace, e-commerce business or travel technology organisation, and familiarity with the seasonality and long purchase cycles that come with them.Breadth in statistical modelling and machine learning, such as regression, classification, clustering and bandits, alongside your experimentation depth.Experience applying AI, Large Language Models, agentic AI or automation to improve analytical productivity and decision-making effectiveness.A reputation for raising the standard of thinking and decision-making in every team you join.Experience with SaaS experimentation tools such as Statsig, Eppo or GrowthBook, or with an in-house platform.

We strive to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please make sure to reach out to your individual recruiter or our team at AccessibleRecruiting@tripadvisor.com.

If you have any additional questions about careers at Tripadvisor you can email us at recruitment@tripadvisor.com. We have all the answers!

To meet the needs of stakeholders/ customers through operational excellence and customer servicePerform prescribed activities in a timely manner and to a high standardNo people leadership roles at this grade.Execute work requirements as identified in processes and procedures, collaborating with and impacting on the work of team members.Identify escalation of policy breaches as required.Take responsibility for customer service and operational execution tasks.Take ownership for managing risk and strengthening controls in relation to the work you own or contribute to. Deliver your work and areas of responsibility in line with relevant rules, regulation and codes of conduct.Gain and maintain an understanding of own role, how the team integrates to achieve overall objectives, alongside knowledge of the work of other teams within the function.Work within well-defined procedures that may involve a variety of work routines.Demonstrate an understanding of the procedures.Evaluate and select the appropriate alternatives from defined options.Make judgements based on the analysis of factual information.Build relationships with stakeholders and customers to identify and address their needs, in support of a smooth operating process, handling sensitive issues as required.

All colleagues will be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Values of Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence and Stewardship – our moral compass, helping us do what we believe is right. They will also be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Mindset – to Empower, Challenge and Drive – the operating manual for how we behave.

Annual Salary £25,200 + benefits

Getting qualified. It's a huge achievement that can completely change your prospects – but it’s not always open to everyone, whether that's due to the cost of university or the timing not being right. But with our apprenticeships, all that can change. Here at Barclays we offer a world-class programme that provides you with a permanent, full-time job with a competitive salary from day one - all whilst gaining a professional qualification at the same time. Whether you're a school-leaver looking for alternative options to the traditional university route or you're someone thinking differently about your future, we'll help you to build an extraordinary career at Barclays, no matter your background.

Our programme is designed for school leavers and career changers, but is open to anyone, no matter your background or your age.

Why a Barclays Apprenticeship?

You’ll get the opportunity to earn whilst working towards a Data Scientist Degree Apprenticeship, a perfect blend of theoretical learning and real-life practical work whilst on a full-time salary in a permanent job. A unique chance to get a professional qualification without the student loan, all whilst getting years of work experience under your belt. Due to the evolving nature of Apprenticeships, a new Apprenticeship might become available and if deemed more relevant to your role, we'll change the Apprenticeship before you start.

We’ve spent over a decade perfecting the support that you’ll receive on our Apprenticeship programme. From day one, you’ll be assigned a Programme Support Manager matched to your needs and background, and together with your People Leader, they’ll support you as an individual. We’ll also match you to an expert in your specialist subject, ready to share their knowledge.

The Apprenticeship route gives you the opportunity for self-discovery and helps you to explore different career paths. With over 325 years of expertise in Banking, Barclays operates in 39 countries, employing around 90,000 people to help move, lend, invest and protect money for customers and clients worldwide.

Why the Operations Apprenticeship programme?

Operations keeps Barclays moving for customers, clients and colleagues. You’ll learn how banking services are delivered, how processes are improved, and how teams work together to manage risk, solve problems and provide excellent service.

Are you eligible?

First, you’ll need the right qualifications. For this apprenticeship opportunity you’ll need 3 A-levels at grades BBC, plus GCSE qualifications in both Maths and English at Grade C (4) or an equivalent qualification.

Beyond that though, we’re also looking for commitment and enthusiasm. Our Apprenticeships place deep investment in you as an individual. That means we need you to match that commitment: you’ll turn up every day ready to work hard, push yourself, and think differently about what you’re capable of.

To apply for our apprentice programme, you must meet the Government's apprentice funding requirements that apply to you.

The Government apprentice funding requirements include a number of requirements that you must meet, including a 3 year residence requirement (subject to certain exceptions). To qualify for the Government's apprentice funding requirements, you must also have the legal right to work for the full duration of the programme at the point of enrolment, with no gaps in your legal right to work or dependency on future visa applications during the period of your apprenticeship (August 2027 to August 2031).

You must also not have undertaken any previous study, education, training, qualifications, or apprenticeship, gained learning or competence from prior work experience, or received prior funding or financial support which renders you ineligible for the Government’s apprentice funding.

Working In London

If you love the buzz of city life, our global HQ is the place to be. Our London hub is in Canary Wharf, at the heart of London’s financial district, with opportunities to explore many functions across a global financial institution.

What happens once you apply?

Step 1 - We'll review your application

Step 2 - You'll be asked to complete our online assessments

Step 3 - We'll ask you to complete a survey, so we can be sure of your eligibility

Step 4 - It's time to attend an in-person assessment day, where you'll be assessed during a group activity and interview (this will take place from October 2026)

Step 5 - We'll let you know the outcome and give you feedback.

It is the policy of Barclays to ensure equal employment opportunity without discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, national origin, alienage or citizenship status, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital or domestic/civil partnership status, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other basis protected by law.

The closing date for applications is 25 September 2026. Please note that this vacancy may close ahead of the advertised date due to application volumes, and we therefore recommend submitting your application as early as possible.

rows.title: Data Scientist
rows.descriptionText:
Location: Hybrid, Monument Place

Reporting to: Insights Lead

Help Shape the Future of Data-Driven Decision Making at GTR

Are you passionate about turning complex data into meaningful insight that drives real-world outcomes?

At GTR, we're looking for an ambitious and forward-thinking Data Scientist to help us unlock the power of data, machine learning and advanced analytics across one of the UK's largest train operating companies.

This is a unique opportunity to play a key role in establishing GTR's first in-house machine learning capability, helping us better understand future risks, opportunities and operational outcomes. You'll work at the heart of our Data & AI function, developing predictive models that support smarter decision making, improve performance and create tangible value for our customers and business.

About The Role

As a Data Scientist in the Central Data & Ai function, you will use advanced analytics, statistical modelling and machine learning techniques to extract forward-looking insights from large and complex datasets across multiple business domains.

Working closely with operational and business stakeholders, you'll help define business problems, test hypotheses and develop predictive and prescriptive models that influence decision making across commercial, operational and safety functions.

This role offers the opportunity to work within a modern enterprise data environment, leveraging over 40 DataHub products that support more than 2,000 active users. As GTR continues to expand its data and AI capabilities, you'll play an important role in shaping standards, approaches and best practices for data science across the organisation.

What You'll Be Doing

Developing predictive and prescriptive models using curated DataHub datasets.Applying statistical and machine learning techniques to identify trends, risks and future outcomes.Working with stakeholders to frame business challenges, define hypotheses and design effective interventions.Translating complex analytical findings into clear, actionable insights for technical and non-technical audiences.Explaining model assumptions, limitations and risks to support informed decision making.Collaborating with Data Engineers to develop data models that support analytical and machine learning use cases.Monitoring, evaluating and improving model performance as business conditions evolve.Contributing to the development of data science standards, governance and best practice across GTR.Supporting the responsible adoption of AI and advanced analytics within an enterprise environment.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for a curious and commercially aware Data Scientist who combines strong technical expertise with excellent stakeholder engagement skills.

You Will Bring

Demonstrable experience delivering end-to-end data science solutions in a business environment.Strong knowledge of statistical modelling, machine learning and predictive analytics techniques.Advanced Python and SQL skills, with experience building scalable analytical solutions for production environments.Experience designing, training, validating and deploying machine learning models.Strong problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to translate complex business challenges into structured analytical approaches.Experience working with large enterprise datasets and integrating multiple data sources to generate actionable insight.Strong data visualisation and storytelling skills, ideally using Power BI or similar tools.Experience working within cloud-based analytics platforms, ideally Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Databricks, Synapse or similar technologies.The ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly and confidently to stakeholders at all levels.A collaborative mindset with the confidence to challenge assumptions and propose innovative solutions.

Qualifications

Degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Why Join Us?

This is an exciting opportunity to help shape the future of data science and AI at GTR.

You'll work on meaningful challenges that directly influence how one of the UK's largest train operating companies serves its customers, manages risk and improves performance. You'll have the chance to build innovative solutions at scale, work with modern technologies and collaborate with colleagues across the business to create lasting impact.

Our culture is built around being Fair, Accountable, Collaborative, Transparent and Open-Minded, while ensuring everyone feels Valued, Respected and Safe. We believe diverse perspectives drive better outcomes and we're committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive.

Ready to Make an Impact?

If you're passionate about using data science, analytics and machine learning to solve complex business challenges and shape better outcomes, we'd love to hear from you.

Join us and help build the future of data-driven decision making at GTR.

Please note that we reserve the right to close this vacancy earlier than the advertised closing date if we receive a high volume of suitable applications.

rows.title: Data Scientist, Experimentation
rows.descriptionText:
About Tripadvisor

The Tripadvisor Group connects people to experiences worth sharing, and aims to be the world’s most trusted source for travel and experiences. We leverage our brands, technology, and capabilities to connect our global audience with partners through rich content, travel guidance, and two-sided marketplaces for experiences, accommodations, restaurants, and other travel categories. The subsidiaries of Tripadvisor, Inc. (Nasdaq: TRIP), include a portfolio of travel brands and businesses, including Tripadvisor, Viator, and TheFork.

At Tripadvisor experiences, the only thing we love more than travel is data. We slice it, we dice it, and we use it to empower our decision making.

What You Will Do

As a Data Scientist on our experimentation team you will work with product teams across Viator to measure whether the changes they ship actually worked, defining the metrics that matter and making sure the decisions that follow are sound.

Part of your contribution is making experimentation easier for the teams you support, through reusable tooling, clear documentation and consistent practice. Viator sells experiences that travellers often book once a year, in a marketplace where supply is finite and shared, so you will be learning to navigate problems where the obvious analysis can give the wrong answer, with support from senior practitioners who have done it before.

You Will

Design and analyse experiments end to end with the product teams you support, working directly with the Product Managers and Engineers who will act on the results.Turn product questions into testable hypotheses with pre-registered primary metrics, appropriate guardrails, and an honest view of what the available traffic can and cannot detect before the experiment starts.Define and instrument feature-level metrics, understanding how metric choice affects sensitivity, interpretation and the decision a team is trying to make.Investigate results properly, checking assignment integrity, exposure and data quality before conclusions are drawn, and treating a surprising result as something to diagnose rather than announce.Build reusable queries, tooling and templates and apply our shared protocols, so teams can run good experiments faster and with less rework.Communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, including inconclusive and negative results, with a recommendation attached rather than a table of numbers.Look beyond whether a change worked to why it worked, and flag when a result may not hold for other users, markets or time periods.Carry out analysis beyond experiments, including opportunity sizing, funnel and behavioural analysis, and observational measurement where randomisation isn't possible.Document hypotheses, designs, outcomes and decisions so results remain comparable and the organisation compounds what it learns.Grow your own depth in experimentation and causal inference, with review and mentorship from senior and principal data scientists.

Skills & Experience

Experience: Solid experience in data science or a similar quantitative role, supporting and influencing product teams.Statistical & Experimentation Foundations: Sound understanding of experimentation beyond running it through a platform, including statistical power and minimum detectable effect, the difference between an inconclusive result and no effect, why peeking and post-hoc metric selection cause problems, and the common ways an experiment can be invalid.Technical & Modelling Expertise: Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, with hands-on experience of statistical analysis and experimentation, and some exposure to statistical modelling or machine learning techniques such as regression and classification.Product Acumen: Ability to define, implement and operationalise product and feature-level metrics, with support from senior colleagues on the most complex cases.Partnership: Experience working closely with Product Managers and Engineers as a trusted partner, and a willingness to make things easier for those teams through tooling, documentation and consistent practice.Critical Thinking: A habit of asking whether a result is trustworthy before asking what it means, and comfort saying so when it isn't.Communication: Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain statistical reasoning to people without a statistical background and to hold your position constructively when a result is unwelcome.Education: Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Data Science, Engineering, Physics, Economics, or a related quantitative field.

You could be an especially great fit if you have:

Experience with metrics that are difficult to measure, such as sparse conversion, heavy-tailed revenue, or slow-to-observe outcomes.Familiarity with variance reduction techniques and why they matter for sensitivity.Exposure to causal inference methods for situations where randomisation isn't available.Experience with SaaS experimentation tools such as Statsig, Eppo or GrowthBook, or with an in-house platform.Experience in a high-scale consumer product environment such as a marketplace, e-commerce or travel platform.An interest in how modern AI tooling can make analysis faster and experimentation more accessible to product teams.

We strive to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please make sure to reach out to your individual recruiter or our team at AccessibleRecruiting@tripadvisor.com.

If you have any additional questions about careers at Tripadvisor you can email us at recruitment@tripadvisor.com. We have all the answers!

rows.title: Data Scientist - Technology Solutions
rows.descriptionText:
Role Overview

We’re looking for a Data Scientist to join our Technology Solutions squad. You’ll develop the models behind our custom-built solutions for sports events and properties, contributing to a growing portfolio of broadcast, digital and fan-facing products delivered via B2C/B2B applications and APIs. You’ll sit within a cross-functional squad and work closely with colleagues across the business, so you’ll need to be comfortable collaborating across disciplines and different technologies.

What You’ll Do

Modelling & Analysis: Develop, train and evaluate models using statistical and machine learning techniques, with a focus on probabilistic approaches. Contribute across the modelling lifecycle from feature engineering and training through to validation and deployment.Data Work: Query, clean and explore datasets using Python and SQL to surface patterns and support model development.Data Pipelines: Help build and maintain the pipelines your models depend on, ingesting and validating new and often messy sports data sources.AI-Assisted Development: Leverage AI tools to accelerate and improve your day-to-day workflow.Event Support: Our solutions are often built around specific sporting events, meaning fixed deadlines and go-live support requirements that you will help to provide.Quality & Rigour: Apply good model development discipline through version control, testing and documentation.

Requirements

What You’ll Bring

Passion for Sport: You follow sport closely and understand the context of the data and audiences we build for. Comfortable with sport-driven modelling decisions.Machine Learning & Statistics: Solid grounding in machine learning, supervised and unsupervised methods, and classical statistical techniques. Comfortable working with probabilistic models, uncertainty estimation and Bayesian inference.Model Development: Understanding of the full model training pipeline, including data preparation, feature selection, model selection and model validation.Experience: Hands-on experience building and evaluating models in a data science or quantitative context.Python & SQL: Comfortable using Python and SQL for data exploration, feature development and modelling workflows.Interest in Data Engineering: An appetite for the engineering side of the work — you want to understand and help own the pipeline that feeds your model, rather than hand that problem to someone else.Client-Centricity & Communication: You keep the client in mind throughout, and can present findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. You’re comfortable explaining your work directly to client stakeholders and translating what they need into modelling decisions.

Nice to Haves

Golf: A passion for golf is a real advantage. A significant share of this squad’s work is golf, so familiarity with strokes gained, shot-level data and how a tournament unfolds will let you contribute quickly.Data Engineering: Experience building and maintaining production data pipelines, or working with AWS services such as Lambda, EventBridge and DynamoDB.Simulation: Experience with Monte Carlo methods or probabilistic simulation.AI Integration: Comfortable using AI-assisted coding tools such as Claude Code or Cursor as part of your everyday workflow, and open to integrating them deeper into how you model and build.

What We Look For

Curiosity: You are naturally curious about the “Why”. You look at data and user behaviour to inform your decisions.Collaborative & Open: You treat your work as a starting point for collaboration. You contribute to shared knowledge and code bases, and work well within a cross-functional team that brings together colleagues from across the business.Client-Centric: You care about the people using what you build. You listen to what clients and stakeholders actually need and let that shape how you approach a problem.Continuous Development: You are keen to develop knowledge and skills, keeping up to date with relevant developments and applying new learning where appropriate.

Benefits

What We Offer

Hybrid working out of our London office (Farringdon) - most of our staff come into the office about three days a weekSalary based on our external benchmarking framework, plus eligibility for a bonus schemePrivate health insurancePersonal days, including birthdays and health and wellness daysAI forward culture

Bristol, Darlington, London, Manchester, Wolverhampton

Job Summary

We are MHCLG

Join our Social Housing Statistics team and play a key role in producing the data and analysis that informs decisions on social housing, affordable housing and housing delivery across England.

As an Analyst, you'll work with a rich case-level dataset covering social housing lettings and sales, helping to deliver high-quality statistics that support policymakers, housing providers and the wider public. This is an excellent opportunity to gain experience across the full statistical production cycle, from data collection and quality assurance through to analysis, publication and user engagement.

You'll collaborate with a wide range of stakeholders, including local authorities, housing associations and policy colleagues, using data to answer important questions about social housing tenancies, tenants and property sales. Your work will directly contribute to improving understanding of the social housing sector and supporting evidence-based decision-making.

You'll be part of the Housing and Planning Statistics team in MHCLG, a friendly, supportive and influential analytical community working on some of the Government's highest-profile housing priorities. We are committed to helping our people grow and develop, offering stretching opportunities, tailored support and the chance to build a rewarding career in analysis and statistics.

This vacancy is for candidates who are not currently members of the Government Statistical Service (GSS) but meet the eligibility criteria to join the profession. 

If you are applying under the GES, GSR or GORS professions, either as a current member or as someone eligible for membership, or if you are already a member of the GSS, please apply to vacancy 481071. 

Job Description

About the role

This role sits within the Social Housing Statistics team, part of MHCLG's central analytical directorate. The team is responsible for collecting, assuring, analysing and publishing data on social housing lettings and sales, providing valuable insights that help shape housing policy and decision-making.

This is a varied and rewarding role offering exposure to the full statistical production cycle. You'll work across data collection, quality assurance, statistical publications, bespoke analysis and stakeholder engagement, making an important contribution to the delivery of high-quality official statistics. The role would suit someone who enjoys working with data, solving complex problems, communicating insights clearly and collaborating with a wide range of stakeholders.

Key responsibilities

As An Analyst In The Team, You Will:

Build strong relationships with data suppliers, including local authorities and housing associations, supporting them to provide high-quality, complete and accurate data.Carry out data validation and quality assurance activities, investigating issues and working with providers to resolve queries and improve data quality.Lead key aspects of the annual quality assurance process, ensuring the data is robust and suitable for inclusion in Accredited Official Statistics publications.Contribute to the production of annual statistical releases by carrying out analysis, drafting outputs and quality assuring the work of colleagues.Produce bespoke analysis to support policy development, ministerial priorities and external information requests, applying appropriate disclosure control techniques where required and developing clear commentary. Help develop and improve the data collection to ensure it continues to meet evolving policy, operational and user needs.Work collaboratively across the team, directorate and wider department, sharing expertise and contributing to continuous improvement and innovation.

In this role, you'll have the opportunity to develop your analytical, technical and stakeholder engagement skills while working on data and statistics that support some of the Government's most important housing priorities.

As An Analyst In The Team, You Will:

Build strong relationships with data suppliers, including local authorities and housing associations, supporting them to provide high-quality, complete and accurate data.Carry out data validation and quality assurance activities, investigating issues and working with providers to resolve queries and improve data quality.Lead key aspects of the annual quality assurance process, ensuring the data is robust and suitable for inclusion in Accredited Official Statistics publications.Contribute to the production of annual statistical releases by carrying out analysis, drafting outputs and quality assuring the work of colleagues.Produce bespoke analysis to support policy development, ministerial priorities and external information requests, applying appropriate disclosure control techniques where required and developing clear commentary. Help develop and improve the data collection to ensure it continues to meet evolving policy, operational and user needs.Work collaboratively across the team, directorate and wider department, sharing expertise and contributing to continuous improvement and innovation.

In this role, you'll have the opportunity to develop your analytical, technical and stakeholder engagement skills while working on data and statistics that support some of the Government's most important housing priorities.

Person specification

Essential Criteria

We're looking for someone who can demonstrate:

The ability to communicate analytical findings and insights clearly and accurately, both verbally and in writing, tailoring messages for non-technical audiences.Effective obtainment and use of data, including assuring its quality and understanding how it can be improved to meet the needs of a variety of users.Strong relationship-building and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively and collaboratively with colleagues, data providers and a range of data users.The ability to work independently, use sound judgement to solve problems, and manage competing priorities to deliver high-quality work.Strong organisational skills, with the flexibility to adapt to changing priorities and work across a varied portfolio of activities.An aptitude for learning and applying analytical and coding tools to support data analysis and statistical production.

Experience of analytical tools such as SQL, Python, R or Power BI would be beneficial. However, we're equally interested in candidates who can demonstrate the ability and enthusiasm to develop these skills and apply them in a data and analytical environment.

Analysts in MHCLG must be affiliated to a government analytical profession. This is usually one of the following:

Government Economic Service (GES) Government Operational Research Service (GORS) Government Social Research Service (GSR) Government Statistical Service (GSS) 

Stage 1: Filter and eligibility questions, entry tests

Candidates who successfully pass the initial filter and eligibility questions will be asked to confirm which of the analytical professions they belong to or are applying to be part of. This information will be used to progress successful applications to the appropriate professional checks element of the process.

Existing civil servants who are currently a member of one of these professions will retain their professional membership in this role. Applicants on promotion will be assessed for promotion within their profession as part of the selection process. Please make any current affiliation clear in your application.

External candidates or civil servants without a current profession affiliation may be considered for accreditation to one of the professions as part of the recruitment process. If you are not currently a member of a government analytical profession you will be put through the membership process for your chosen profession as part of this application. You must pass the membership process for your application to be successful. If you do not pass the relevant profession entry test your application will not be taken further. See the Guide for Analytical Candidates document for more details of the membership process for the relevant profession.

Entry Qualifications 

The entry qualifications are listed below. Please list FULL details of your degree in your application form.

Government Statistical Service (GSS):

You must meet one of the following criteria:

Hold a first or second class honours degree in a numerate subject (2:1 minimum for Assistant Statistician and 2:2 minimum for Statistical Officer), containing at least 25% taught statistical content (e.g. statistics, mathematics, economics, sciences, business studies, psychology, geography or similar); Hold a higher degree (e.g. MSc or PhD) in a subject containing formal statistical training (e.g. statistics, mathematics, economics, sciences, business studies, psychology, geography or similar); Have worked in a statistical or data science field and be able to demonstrate continuous professional development (via a logbook) in statistics or data science at the same level as a foundation degree or Higher National Diploma (level five); Have achieved, or be on track to achieve, a Level 4 apprenticeship, including at least two years in a statistical or data analysis role in government, and be able to demonstrate continuous professional development in statistics or data analysis (via a logbook signed off by a manager or mentor who is a member of the statistical profession).

rows.title: Environmental Data Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Job Description

Environmental Data Analyst

About Us

Tradeweb is a global leader in electronic trading across asset classes. As financial markets become increasingly interconnected, our technology enables efficient, multi-asset trading on a global scale. We serve more than 3,000 clients in more than 85 countries, including many of the world’s largest banks, asset managers, hedge funds, insurers, corporations, and wealth managers.

Creative collaboration and sharp client focus have helped fuel our organic growth. We facilitated average daily trading volume (ADV) of more than $2.8 trillion over the past four fiscal quarters, topping $3.3 trillion in ADV for the first quarter of 2026.

Since our IPO in 2019, Tradeweb has completed four acquisitions and doubled our revenues – and 2025 was our 26th consecutive year of record revenues.

The Opportunity

We are recruiting an Environmental Data Analyst to support the preparation, maintenance and assurance of our greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory. This is a data-driven role: the organisation reports emissions across multiple cycles each year, to more than one set of stakeholders and under more than one assurance process, and the analyst keeps that data accurate, traceable and on time.

The role centers on four areas: data collection and validation across GHG inventory books; book maintenance, estimation and reconciliation; assurance evidence preparation; and controlled automation of repetitive analyses. The analyst independently executes clearly defined workstreams, while the inventory owner retains responsibility for methodology, quality control and final sign-off.

What You’ll Do

 Data collection and validation – run the multi-cycle collection process across GHG inventory, covering several hundred data points; validate figures, investigate prior-year and variance discrepancies, and keep internal data providers internal teams engaged and responsive.  Book maintenance, estimation and reconciliation – maintain the GHG inventory and the supporting carbon accounting systems; assist in producing interim full-year estimates from part-year data, reconcile to actuals, document variances and maintain version control so the correct figures reach the correct audience.  Assurance evidence preparation – prepare evidence and documentation for multiple external assurance processes, support walkthroughs, respond to queries and keep the full inventory and methodology documentation at an assurance-ready standard year-round.  Controlled automation – build and maintain tooling that automates repetitive analyses such as business travel, office attendance and ledger clean-up, and improve datasets, dashboards and reporting processes to strengthen data quality. 

About You

 Prior relevant experience in data analysis, sustainability reporting, environmental data or a related area.  Advanced proficiency in Excel, with experience managing, analysing and reconciling large datasets.  A strong data orientation – comfortable working with large datasets, spotting anomalies building repeatable, well-controlled processes.  Working knowledge of the GHG Protocol (basic or university-level is sufficient) and a interest or experience in sustainability reporting.  Confidence using technology and AI to automate repeatable work and build reliable tooling around routine analyses.  Strong attention to detail, initiative and reliability: able to take a task from instruction through to completion in a deadline-driven cycle, escalating issues where necessary.  A self-starter who is organised and capable of working independently while collaborating with global stakeholders. 

Why join Tradeweb?

Your work will help Tradeweb understand its environmental footprint and give stakeholders confidence in the information we report. You’ll have the opportunity to make lasting improvements to how we manage emissions data across our global business, tackling complex data challenges and seeing the difference your work makes to our environmental reporting.

At Tradeweb, our values guide how we work: we share ideas, stay curious, take ownership, exceed expectations, act responsibly and embrace differences. Together, they create a collaborative and inclusive environment where everyone can contribute and succeed.

Benefits

We offer a comprehensive range of benefits designed to support our employees at every stage of life and career. These include enhanced parental leave, family-building and postpartum support through Maven, subsidised gym membership and a wide range of learning and development opportunities.

Specific offerings vary by location, and our team can provide further information about the benefits available to you during the recruitment process.

Additional Information

Business area: Sustainability

Role level: Associate

Contract term: Permanent

Location: London – hybrid working, with 1-2 days per week on-site

Applications: Open to internal and external applicants

rows.title: Revenue Management Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Location: CrossCountry Trains | Hybrid Working | Typically based at the Birmingham Office (3 days a week) and Work from Home (2 days a week)

Salary: £37,000

At CrossCountry Trains, we aim to be an industry-leading, customer-focused, and innovative long-distance train operator. We are committed to building a sustainable railway that connects all major cities outside of London, delivering exceptional service that our customers can trust.

About The Role

As a Revenue Management Analyst, you will play a pivotal role in driving the commercial success of CrossCountry Trains while enhancing the customer experience.

This is a unique opportunity to manage a key CrossCountry route, influence strategic decisions, and pioneer innovative revenue management techniques that directly shape how thousands of passengers travel every day. If you thrive in a dynamic, data-driven environment and want to be part of a forward-thinking company committed to sustainable growth and exceptional service, this role is for you.

Key Responsibilities

Effectively managing price and seat availability, interpreting short term demand and supply data to adjust availability of discounted ticket quotas to maximise revenue and minimise overcrowding (inventory control, or yield/revenue management)Extract and interpret key data available to identify opportunities and areas of improvement for your assigned route. Propose actions to mitigate risks and capitalise on opportunities, implementing strategies and perform monitoring.Use revenue management systems to manage and automate business policies for a portfolio of trains in terms of loadings, reservations, revenue, and competition, including managing performance against agreed targets and performance indicators.Review feedback on crowding and reservations from wider business and implement actions, as necessary.Assist in producing weekly and periodic reporting to be shared internally within the wider commercial team as well as externally within the organisation.Act as a commercial partner for a region, providing insight and recommendations as well as gathering feedback and suggestions on how to improve revenue in that area.

About You

Essential Skills and Experience

A strong understanding of revenue management concepts, theories, techniques, and related systems.Experience of presenting and communicating numerical information in a simple and powerful manner to a wide audience.Excellent analytical skills with experience working with large datasets, meeting KPIs, and identifying trends and opportunities.Good understanding of Microsoft Office products such as Power BI and other analytical and statistical tools like Tableau.Demonstrated understanding of SQL, with good working knowledge of Python for data processing, analysis, and workflow automation.Good communicator and ability to work alone or as part of a team.Proactive, commercially minded, and passionate about data-driven revenue optimisation.

Desirable Skills And Experience

Undergraduate on a business, statistics, or operational degree course.Understanding of revenue management concepts, theories and techniques, and related systems.Understanding of railway geography and pricing strategies.

Employee Benefits

Employee Assistance Programme.Free Rail Travel on all CrossCountry and Arriva owned train companies.Discounted travel on UK and European trains.Pension Scheme.Cycle to Work Scheme.

We believe in the power of diversity and inclusion and are committed to building a workforce that reflects the varied backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives of our society. Your unique talents are welcomed here, and we encourage applications from all backgrounds.

Closing date for applications: 9th October 2026.
