rows.title: Data Automation Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Company Overview:Cerulli Associates (CA) is a research and consulting firm, headquartered in Boston, specializing in product and distribution analysis for the global asset management industry. Since 1992, we have blended primary research and data analysis to bring perspective to current market conditions and forecasts for future developments. With a suite of research publications, an interactive data platform, and custom research and consulting offerings, we provide financial services firms with unparalleled guidance in strategic positioning and new business development.
Cerulli Associates is a 2023, 2024, and 2025 Boston Globe Top Places to Work. We are proud to be recognized for our outstanding employee engagement, management, work-life balance, and benefits.
Our clients include virtually all the top 50 global asset management firms, as well as industry service providers, management consulting companies, banks, broker/dealers, insurance companies, investment consulting firms, and private equity firms.
Position Overview:The Data Automation Analyst will help expand and strengthen Cerulli Associates’ data automation capabilities. Their primary focus will be on reusable data-processing, benchmarking, reporting, and validation workflows that support the firm’s research, publishing, and consulting work.
The successful candidate will combine hands-on technical implementation with careful analytical judgment. This person will work within an evolving modern data environment, contribute to the adoption of stronger data and development practices, and help improve the reliability, scalability, and usability of Cerulli’s data products and workflows. This role will help strengthen the reliable, reusable data foundation needed for analytics, automation, and emerging AI-enabled capabilities.
This role is designed for someone with experience working with real business data and recurring workflows who wants to grow from strong implementation into greater technical ownership and solution development. The position reports to the Associate Director, Data Strategy, and is based in the Boston office. Cerulli operates a hybrid work model, with employees working in the office two days per week.
Responsibilities and Duties:Build, run, validate, and improve reusable data automation and reporting workflowsUse Python and SQL to transform, reconcile, and prepare data for analysis and business deliverablesContribute to cloud-based data pipelines, transformation models, notebooks, and configuration-driven processesDevelop and improve automated checks, regression tests, diagnostics, and validation proceduresInvestigate data and workflow issues through structured root-cause analysis and implement practical correctionsStandardize and align data across reporting periods to support consistent historical analysisMaintain clear technical documentation, process guides, configuration files, and data definitionsPartner with research analysts, Editorial, survey specialists, IT, and other stakeholders to understand workflow requirements and validate outputsIdentify recurring issues, edge cases, and opportunities that should become shared logic, tests, or reusable enhancementsCompare implementation options, communicate tradeoffs, and constructively identify risks, gaps, or assumptions requiring reviewSupport selected improvements to data access, data products, pipeline performance, and AI-assisted data experiences as priorities evolve
Qualifications:Bachelor’s degree in computer science, data analytics, information systems, statistics, or a related field2 to 4 years of relevant professional experience in data analytics, data engineering, process automation, business intelligence, or a related field; candidates with at least 1 year of especially relevant experience may be consideredStrong fundamentals in Python and SQLAbility to troubleshoot systematically and communicate findings clearlyAbility to collaborate with technical and nontechnical stakeholders, ask effective questions, and challenge assumptions constructivelyExperience with dbt, Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake, Git, or similar data platforms and development practices is preferredExperience with survey data, longitudinal data, wide datasets, configurable reporting, or automated document generation is preferredExperience with financial services, market research, publishing, consulting, or data products is a plus
Salary:$80,000 – $100,000

rows.title: Data Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Position Description

TSD Mobility Solutions, Inc., an affiliate of Reynolds and Reynolds, is looking for a Data Analyst to join our growing team. In this role, you will turn sales, revenue, and margin data into dashboards and executive reports that leadership relies on; own the team's operational automations; and maintain the configuration behind TSD's payments platform. You will be responsible for monthly sales reporting and rep attribution hygiene by maintaining payments reporting (including rate, margin pools, and volume trends). You will build pivot-ready datasets, macros, and automated workflows in Excel, Power Query, and Google Sheets, and take ownership of existing automations that report team stats.

Responsibilities Will Include, But Are Not Limited To

Take ownership of existing automations that report team stats.Route escalations and handle metadata attribution.Manage monthly payments account maintenance, including pricing adjustments and configuration updates.Flag anomalies affecting billing or margin.Maintain, troubleshoot, and extend these automations as reporting and operational needs evolve.Build repeatable workflows to extract cost, interchange, and margin insights from raw merchant processor statements.

Training

About Stellix

Stellix helps organizations in the life sciences and other critical industries connect strategy, systems, and teams so they can turn digital and AI investments into measurable operational results. Join our team as we design, implement, and govern the adaptive operating models that produce outcomes that matter to our clients and the communities they serve.

Role Summary

We are seeking a motivated recent college graduate to join our team and help accelerate the application of AI across Stellix’s enterprise knowledge platform. This is a hands-on, entry-level role for someone who is curious about how AI can transform the way a consulting and engineering firm captures, organizes, and reuses its institutional expertise.

Stellix’s knowledge platform is built on Glean and connects SharePoint, Teams, OneDrive, Confluence, Salesforce, Smartsheet, and other enterprise systems into a unified search, AI assistant, and agent environment. The long-term vision is to build a compounding knowledge platform that captures expertise from every engagement and turns it into reusable intellectual property — so each project makes the next project better.

As an AI Knowledge Platform Associate, you will work alongside our IT, Digital Platforms, and business teams to build, test, and refine Glean agents; structure and curate knowledge content; support AI workflow development; and help drive adoption across the organization. You will gain hands-on experience with enterprise AI tools, agentic workflows, and knowledge management while contributing to real business outcomes.

This is an ideal role for a recent graduate who is excited about applied AI, comfortable working across technical and business contexts, and eager to learn how AI works inside a real consulting and engineering organization.

Key Responsibilities

Agent Building & Refinement

Build, test, and refine Glean agents that automate multi-step workflows such as contract review, proposal development, knowledge retrieval, and document generation.Translate business requirements into clear agent instructions, step logic, and workflow configurations.Evaluate agent outputs for accuracy, relevance, and alignment with business needs, and iterate on prompts and configurations to improve quality.Document agent designs, use cases, and operating instructions so they can be maintained and scaled.

Knowledge Structure & Curation

Help organize, tag, and structure content across connected data sources (SharePoint, Confluence, Salesforce, Smartsheet, etc.) to improve search relevance and AI-assisted retrieval.Support the development of Glean Collections and curated knowledge groupings that make expertise easier to find and reuse.Assist in identifying knowledge gaps and working with subject matter experts to fill them.Contribute to the ongoing effort to convert workflows, implementation patterns, and operational learnings into structured, reusable IP.

AI Workflow & Solution Support

Support the design and delivery of AI-enabled workflows using Glean, Microsoft Copilot, Power Automate, and related platforms.Assist in building rapid prototypes and pilots that demonstrate value quickly.Help evaluate new AI features and capabilities as they are released across the platform.Participate in testing and quality assurance for new agents, workflows, and AI features before deployment.

Adoption & Enablement

Support the “Learn More About AI” recurring series by helping prepare demos, examples, and training materials.Assist with user onboarding to the Glean platform, including setup guidance and feature walkthroughs.Gather user feedback, identify friction points, and help translate them into improvement actions.Contribute to internal communications that highlight AI wins and encourage broader adoption.

Governance & Documentation

Follow established AI governance processes, content-handling rules, and guardrails for all work on the platform.Help maintain documentation of agents, workflows, data sources, and permissions.Support audit readiness by ensuring configurations are well-documented and aligned with enterprise standards.

Bachelor’s degree (recent graduate or graduating by start date) in Information Systems, Computer Science, Data Science, Business Analytics, Engineering, or a related field.Strong academic record with coursework or projects involving AI, machine learning, data management, or enterprise systems.

The New England Centenarian Study and Long Life Family Study, based at Boston University School of Medicine seeks a Research Specialist (RS)to be responsible for collection and management of study participant data. The Research Specialist will receive standardized training in conducting and scoring the following measures and will work toward certification in these measures in order to perform them independently. The Research Specialist will be trained and certified in administration of the neuropsychological assessment, Short Physical Performance Battery, vitals and anthropometry assessment, neuromotor exam, carotid ultrasound, blood sample processing, phlebotomy, and video visit administration and technical troubleshooting, as needed by the study. They will obtain vital signs measures, conduct cognitive testing, perform carotid ultrasounds, administer physical function assessments, troubleshoot technology, and draw blood, if interested, or coordinate phlebotomy and stool collection with lab agencies. After each visit, the research specialist will score the cognitive data, process digital cognitive and physical function data and will assist with periodic data quality control efforts. The RS receives a list of data that have been flagged for review. The RS determine whether followup questions are required from the participant and collect the necessary information to resolve the error, whether the data were entered incorrectly, or whether the flagged values are valid data outside the typical range. Additionally, the RS will obtain annual follow-up data via mailed and telephone-administered questionnaires. The position is located in Boston, MA. Schedule is Monday-Friday, typically 9:00am-5:00pm but varies depending on daily schedule to accommodate participants. Occasional Saturdays required (3-4 in Spring and 3-4 in Fall). Travel to participants' homes to conduct offsite examinations and coordination of travel logistics for multiple visits may be required. Previous phlebotomy experience is highly desirable though willingness to take part in a phlebotomy course to learn these skills is also acceptable. Spanish fluency is a plus. The RS works one-on-one with participants without supervision to perform assessments and collect data. rows.title: Center for Digital Mental Health Clinical Research Coordinator
rows.descriptionText:
Site: The General Hospital Corporation

Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not-for-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.

Job Summary

The Department of Psychiatry's Center for Digital Mental Health (CDMH Director: Sabine Wilhelm, Ph.D.) at Massachusetts General Hospital is seeking qualified college graduates with a background in psychology, neuroscience, social work, or a related field to fill Clinical Research Coordinator (CRC) positions. CDMH studies evidence-based technology solutions to prevent, assess, and treat mental illness (e.g., depression, anxiety) and to promote mental health.

This position would be shared between two programs of research: (i) global mental health and (ii) generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tool development for clinical care.

About

First, Dr. Anushka Patel leads a program of global mental health research, with a focus on scalable interventions for trauma-affected populations and suicide prevention. She is currently developing and testing a single-session intervention with chatbot support for domestic violence survivors. Additionally, she is developing a clinical service for suicide prevention in primary care. You can learn more about her work through her profile (link below). This work uses mixed methods, is interdisciplinary, and relies on community-based participatory research methods. The promising applicant will have the following interests and abilities:

 Interest and passion for supporting public health locally and globally Experience with program management is a major strength Experience working in low-resource settings (e.g., LMIC or domestic settings) Familiarity with community psychology and/or public health models is a plus Prior experience with interviewing participants is a plus Direct qualitative research experience is a plus

Second, Dr. Wilhelm leads an innovative research team at the intersection of artificial intelligence, digital technology, and mental health care. The CRC will contribute to the development, evaluation, and implementation of cutting-edge AI-powered tools and digital interventions designed to improve mental health treatment and access to care.

This role offers a unique opportunity to work in a multidisciplinary team alongside clinicians, researchers, data scientists, and patient stakeholders on projects that leverage emerging technologies to address real-world mental health challenges. Responsibilities may include participant recruitment, project management, data collection and analysis, user testing, stakeholder engagement, evaluation of tools and study procedures, and collaboration on the design and refinement of digital mental health platforms and AI-enabled applications.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, diligent, intellectually curious, detail-oriented, and excited about the potential of technology to transform mental health care. Prior experience in clinical research, psychology, public health, human-computer interaction, data science, or digital health is welcome but not required.

This is an exciting opportunity for applicants interested in how advances in AI and digital technology can be responsibly leveraged to improve mental health outcomes and expand access to effective care.

In general, the CRC will serve as the primary liaison between patients, providers, and recruiting studies in the center. The CRC will frequently relay clinical and research information and directly resolve patient issues per the provider's instructions. The patient population is high acuity with complex psychiatric disorders, co-morbid medical problems, substance use, and overlapping psychosocial concerns. The CRC will work as part of a dynamic team of clinicians, researchers, professional staff, and other CRCs to ensure the highest quality of care and service to patients and their clinicians.

The position requires great discretion and judgment to manage sensitive information and effectively prioritize tasks. This challenging and rewarding role would suit a self-motivated individual who enjoys multitasking, possesses excellent communication skills, and is detail-oriented. The CRC will monitor the pace and progress of recruitment to our research studies and serve as the primary point of contact for study participants. The CRC will ensure that all components of the participants' assessments and surveys are appropriately completed and tracked in the computer database.

Qualifications

Principal duties and responsibilities:

 Collects and organizes patient data Maintains records and databases Uses software programs to generate graphs and reports Assists with recruiting patients for studies (e.g., via social media) Obtains patient study data from medical records, physicians, etc. Conduct literature searches Verifies the accuracy of study forms Updates study forms per protocol Documents patient visits and procedures Assists with regulatory binders and QA/QC procedures Assists with interviewing study participants Administers and scores questionnaires Provides a basic explanation of the study, and in some cases, obtains informed consent from participants Assists with study regulatory submissions Writes consent forms Verifies participant inclusion/exclusion criteria Performs administrative support duties as required

A Clinical Research Coordinator II performs the duties of a Clinical Research Coordinator I (above) and may also:

 Maintain research data, patient fields, regulatory binders, and study databases Perform data analysis and QA/QC data checks Organize and interpret data Develop and implement recruitment strategies Act as a study resource for patients and family Monitor and evaluate lab and procedure data Evaluate study questionnairesEvaluate study procedures Contribute to protocol recommendations Assist with the preparation of the annual review Assist PI in preparing study reports

Education

A bachelor’s degree is required with a background in psychology, neuroscience, social work, or a related field.

Experience

New graduates with relevant course/project work experience but without prior research experience will be considered for the Clinical Research Coordinator I position outlined above.

Those with a minimum of 1-2 years of directly related work experience will be considered for a Clinical Research Coordinator II position.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

 Careful attention to details Strong organizational skills Ability to follow directions Ability to multitask Excellent written and oral communication skills Computer literacy Working knowledge of research methods Ability to demonstrate respect and professionalism for participants’ rights and individual needs Strong interpersonal skills, especially when working with people across cultures Ability to both work independently (i.e., self-motivated) and as part of a team (i.e., a collaborative team member), and be able to ask for support when needed

The Clinical Research Coordinator II Should Also Possess

 Ability to work independently and as a team player Analytical skills and ability to resolve technical problems Ability to interpret the acceptability of data results Working knowledge of data management programs

To apply, please submit your resume/CV and a cover letter. Please list your GPA (cumulative and major) and relevant coursework on your resume/CV.

rows.descriptionText:
Job Title: 2027 Spring Co-op mRNA Drug Substance Process Characterization Data Analytics and Visualization

Grade: Co-opLocation: Waltham, MADuration: 6 months


About The Job

Looking to launch your career at the cutting edge of healthcare? Join Sanofi for a chance to develop with mentoring and guidance from inspirational leaders while helping to make an impact on the lives of countless people worldwide. We are seeking a highly motivated Spring Co-op to join our mRNA Drug Substance Process Characterization Data Analytics and Visualization team.

This role focuses on developing tools and workflows to analyze, visualize, and streamline analytical data generated in support of mRNA drug substance process development. You will work closely with a team of scientists responsible for routine and development-stage analytical assays, including HPLC, LCMS, ELISA, qPCR, and electrophoretic methods. The primary goal of this internship is to improve how analytical data is processed, interpreted, and communicatedenabling faster decision-making and increased throughput. This is a hands-on role at the intersection of analytical chemistry/biochemistry and data science, with opportunities to directly impact development decisions, lab operations, assay performance tracking, and data integrity.

Ready to grow your skills while helping shape the future of healthcare? At Sanofi, youll be empowered to learn, ask questions, and bring your ideas to life all while supported by inspiring mentors and collaborative teams.

About Sanofi

Were an R&D-driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving peoples lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system and innovative pipeline enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve peoples lives.

Main Responsibilities

Design and implement data analysis and visualization tools for analytical datasets (e.g., HPLC, LCMS, ELISA, qPCR).Build automated workflows for data ingestion, cleaning, and transformation from instrument outputs or shared databases.Develop intuitive data visualization dashboards (e.g. Power BI) for assay output, performance, trends, and control.Support statistical analysis of assay performance (e.g., accuracy, precision, linearity).Collaborate with scientists to understand pain points and translate them into practical data-based solutions.Document tools and workflows for internal use and scalability.


About You

Basic Qualifications:

Currently pursuing a Masters or PhD in: Biochemistry, Chemical Biology, Analytical Chemistry, Bioengineering, Data Science, or related field.Must be permanently authorized to work in the U.S. and not require sponsorship of an employment visa (e.g., H-1B or green card) at the time of application or in the future. Students currently on CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT usually require future sponsorship for long term employment and do not meet the Internal requirements for this program unless eligible for an alternative long-term status that does not require company sponsorship.Must be enrolled in an accredited college or university throughout the duration of the co-op/internship.Must be able to relocate to the office location and work 40hrs/week, Monday to Friday for the full duration of the co-op/internship.


PreferredQualifications

Strong quantitative background with experience in data analysis, statistics and visualization.Proficiency in at least one of the following: Python (pandas, numpy, matplotlib/seaborn, plotly), R (tidyverse, ggplot2) and MATLAB.Ability to work with structured and semi-structured data.Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.Effective communication skills, with the ability to translate technical results to non-experts.Experience working with analytical laboratory data, such as: Chromatography (HPLC/UPLC)/ LCMS/ or plate-based assaysFamiliarity with analytical software platforms (e.g., Chromeleon, OpenLab, MassHunter, SoftMax Pro).Experience with scientific data pipelines or ETL workflows.Knowledge of assay validation principles (e.g., ICH Q2 guidelines)Experience with: Building dashboards (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, Dash, Streamlit), time-series analysis or process monitoring and handling large datasets or high-throughput workflows.Exposure to biologics or mRNA-related analytical methods.Interest in laboratory operations, automation, or workflow optimization.


Why Choose Us

Bring the miracles of science to life alongside a supportive, future focused team.Stretch your skills through apprenticeships, internships, graduate programs, and international experiences that grow with you.Learn from inspiring mentors and collaborative teams while contributing to real projects that shape the future of healthcare.Build your future with access to the latest tools, digital innovation, and continuous learning that keep you ahead of the curve.


Compensation

The salary range for this position is$35.00 -$58.00hourly. All compensation will be determined commensurate with demonstrated experience.

rows.title: AI Foundations - Research Scientist - Research Internship - 2027
rows.descriptionText:
Introduction

Join the pioneering AI Foundations Research team at IBM Research and contribute to shaping the future foundations of artificial intelligence. Our group of scientists, engineers, and designers is dedicated to conducting end-to-end research that delivers real-world AI impact through a rigorous, responsible, and open innovation framework. We are the team behind IBM's Granite open-source models, and our work spans multi-modal (vision, speech, language, code) and multi-lingual systems, data quality, data generation, novel model architectures, training recipes, governance and trustworthiness, and programming models for interacting with models. As an intern, you will explore cutting-edge research areas, including new algorithms for training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and inference time scaling, alongside pioneering work in generative computing and generative programming for language, code, and other modalities, all within a collaborative environment that bridges fundamental science and transformative engineering.

Your Role And Responsibilities

As an AI Research Scientist Intern, you will engage in the full research lifecycle to pioneer new advancements in artificial intelligence. Your role will involve identifying core challenges, designing novel prototype solutions, and validating them through rigorous experimentation. You will conduct foundational research in critical areas such as novel training algorithms, efficient fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and inference-time scaling for multi-modal models. Collaborating in small, mentored teams, you will be responsible for shepherding projects from ideation to completion. A key objective is to disseminate significant results through publications in leading conferences and patent applications, contributing to both the academic community and IBM's open innovation initiatives.

Preferred Education

Master's Degree

Required Technical And Professional Expertise

Research Experience with Modern ML: Hands-on experience with and a deep theoretical understanding of Large Language Models (LLMs), Vision-Language Models (VLMs), and Transformer-based architectures.Strong Programming & Prototyping Skills: Proficiency in Python for rapid prototyping, experimental setup, and implementing large-scale machine learning systems.Rigorous Analytical & Problem-Solving Abilities: Demonstrated strength in quantitative analysis, designing experiments, and deconstructing complex research problems.Proven Research & Communication Skills: A track record of innovation (evidenced by peer-reviewed publications or strong preprints) and the ability to clearly articulate complex technical concepts in both writing and presentations.Collaborative Research Mindset: A team-oriented approach with a commitment to rigorous, reproducible, and well-documented research practices.

Preferred Technical And Professional Experience

Research Excellence: Strong publication record in top-tier conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, AAAI).Technical Proficiency: Advanced expertise in ML frameworks (PyTorch) and full-cycle development of algorithms and systems.Specialized Skills: Hands-on experience with generative AI (LLMs) and multimodal models, from training to testing.Communication: Demonstrated ability to present complex research and build high-impact technical demonstrations.

rows.title: Associate Data Scientist
rows.descriptionText:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

MITRE’s Systems Performance and Evaluation Department is charged to solve some of our nation's most critical challenges in delivering services to citizens throughout defense and intelligence, aviation, homeland security, the judiciary, healthcare, and cybersecurity domains.

Job Description:

This is an opportunity for an Associate Data Scientist with an interest in advancing and applying innovative data science and analytical techniques to help solve some of our nation's most critical challenges. We are looking for highly motivated, adaptive, and self-directed candidates with motivation to join our technical workforce, expand their technical skills and capabilities, and grow our work supporting the development and deployment of nationally important solutions through Analytics, Data Science, Machine Learning, Model-Based Systems Engineering, Digital Engineering, Systems Architecture and Requirements Engineering, and System-of-Systems and Systems Thinking practices.

As an Associate Data Scientist, you will leverage and grow your analytical, mathematical, data science, and systems engineering expertise to support the analysis, design, implementation, and integration of enterprise systems and systems-of-systems, as well as mission analysis for federal agencies.

Specific responsibilities may include:

Using your understanding of data science, systems and mission engineering, quantitative methods, and an awareness of sponsor needs to determine areas where MITRE can have an impactApplying modern methods and tools such as Data Science, Machine Learning, Data Analytics, Model-Based Systems Engineering, Digital Engineering, Mission Engineering, and Mathematical Modeling to assess capability needs, requirements, architectures, designs, performance constraints and gaps, proposed changes, and verification and test approachesEvaluating and comparing alternative architectures and approaches using qualitative and quantitative techniques; exploring large trade-spaces and analyzing trade-offsIdentifying and developing metrics and analytical methods to measure and analyze relevant system and data properties, such as robustness, resiliency, interoperability, quality, and maintainabilitySupporting requirements management, interface management, and architecture change management processesPerforming data analysis, modeling, and system design and development, including software development, systems modernization, and architectureSupporting multiple tasks across several government-sponsored projects in a small- to large-team environment

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related technical fieldFamiliarity with programming languages and analytical tools such as Python and MATLABFamiliarity with Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) and Digital Engineering (DE) conceptsExperience with statistical analysis, data analysis, and modelingInterest in complex, multi-disciplinary data and analytical problemsWillingness and ability to learn new tools and concepts in a variable environment of government sponsorsMust be eligible to obtain and maintain a Secret U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance.This position requires a minimum of 3 days a week on-site. 

Preferred Qualifications:

Preference given to qualified candidates with active clearanceAdvanced degree in related field of studyExperience with multi-disciplinary modeling and simulation (physics-level, engineering-level and/or socio-technical-level)Experience with Digital Engineering integration through internship, research, or academic projects

This requisition requires the candidate to have a minimum of the following clearance(s):

None

This requisition requires the hired candidate to have or obtain, within one year from the date of hire, the following clearance(s):

Secret

Salary compensation range and midpoint:

$80,000 - $100,000 - $120,000 Annual

Work Location Type:

Onsite

It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.

Commitment to Non-Discrimination

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to disability, status as a protected veteran or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, local or international law.

rows.title: Research Scientist, ML Systems - PhD New College Grad 2026
rows.descriptionText:
Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world.

We are now looking for a Research Scientist New Graduate with a focus on Machine Learning Systems (MLSys). NVIDIA Research is seeking exceptional systems researchers to contribute to the development of hardware, software, and infrastructure technology for ML systems of all scales. Advances in AI/ML heavily rely on the development of efficient, scalable, resilient, and trustworthy systems for training, fine-tuning, and serving ML models. AI/ML applications are also pushing the limits of both personal devices and warehouse-scale data centers. All layers of AI systems need to be co-designed and co-optimized to maximize performance and energy efficiency, improve scalability, and support emerging algorithms in this space. We are seeking candidates that have a proven track record of research excellence, a broad perspective on systems design across the full hardware/software/infrastructure stack, and depth in one of the layers such as AI/ML systems, operating systems, distributed systems, data management, cloud computing, and computer architecture.

What You'll Be Doing

Understand and analyze the efficiency, scaling, and resilience challenges in ML systems, algorithms, and applications. Develop creative systems solutions (hardware, software, infrastructure) for future ML systems of all scales. Contribute to the co-design of next-generation AI/ML algorithms and systems. Collaborate with a diverse set of research and product teams across the company, spanning software, hardware, AI, and networking.Publish original research and speak at conferences and events.

What We Need To See

Recent graduate with a Ph.D. in CS/CE/EE with a strong background in operating systems, distributed systems, inference and training systems, data management systems, networking, cloud computing, and/or computer architecture (or equivalent experience). A strong publication, patent, and research collaboration history is a huge advantage.Demonstrated expertise in one specific area with the ability to become the go-to resource within a team having varied backgrounds.Background with experimental research and development.Experience with C, C++, Python, and/or scripting languages.Experience with using AI tools for analysis, design, and code development.

rows.title: Science Teaching Opportunities
rows.descriptionText:
POTENTIAL INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR INSTRUCTIONAL ASSIGNMENTS

Program: Science Instructor Opportunities

Location: On-site at partner schools; varies by assignment

Teaching Mode: In Person

Grade Levels: Elementary, Middle, and High School; varies by assignment

Schedule: Typically 1–4 instructional service hours per week after school

Program Length: Commonly approximately 10 weeks per assignment

Start Dates: Opportunities become available throughout the school year

Compensation: Typical compensation of $50+ per completed instructional service hour, depending on assignment scope, experience, location, schedule, and agreed compensation

About The Opportunity

Concorde Education is seeking independent instructional contractors to provide engaging, hands-on science enrichment services for K–12 students.

This is a potential independent contractor assignment, not an employee position. Contractors may choose whether to apply for, accept, decline, or ignore available opportunities.

Assignments vary by school, grade level, schedule, curriculum, available materials, available technology, and program objectives.

Concorde may provide curriculum guidance, lesson-plan suggestions, activity ideas, instructional resources, or program objectives. Contractors may use their professional judgment to adapt instruction within the assignment scope and applicable site requirements.

ASSIGNMENT SCOPE

Depending On The Accepted Assignment, Contractors May

 Plan and facilitate engaging, age-appropriate science enrichment sessions; Introduce students to scientific concepts through safe, hands-on experiments, demonstrations, investigations, and project-based learning; Adapt activities based on student experience levels, site requirements, available materials, and program objectives; Guide students through observation, experimentation, data collection, critical thinking, and scientific inquiry, where applicable; Maintain a safe, respectful, inclusive, and age-appropriate learning environment; Communicate assignment-related needs or significant concerns with Concorde and school staff, as appropriate; Complete a brief session completion form after each scheduled session; and Follow applicable site safety, visitor, technology, emergency, and student-protection procedures.

EXAMPLE PROGRAM TOPICS

Assignments May Include Topics Such As

 Everyday chemistry using safe household materials; States of matter and simple chemical reactions; Kitchen science and food chemistry; Cleaning science and how soaps and surfactants work; Simple machines, force, and motion; Engineering and design challenges using common household materials; Environmental science, recycling, ecosystems, energy, and sustainability; Observation, experimentation, measurement, and the scientific method; and Scientific reasoning, problem-solving, and STEM exploration.

Specific content, curriculum requirements, experiments, and instructional resources vary by assignment.

Qualifications

Preferred qualifications include:

 At least 60 college credits, where required by the applicable assignment or site; Experience teaching, tutoring, coaching, mentoring, or leading activities with school-age students; Comfort explaining age-appropriate science concepts through engaging, hands-on instruction; Strong communication, organization, and classroom facilitation skills; Availability to provide services for the accepted assignment schedule and communicate schedule issues as soon as reasonably practicable; and Familiarity with classroom technology, Chromebooks, web-based educational platforms, or related instructional tools.

Preferred backgrounds may include educators, science teachers, STEM professionals, college or graduate students studying science or education, tutors, camp counselors, engineers, healthcare professionals, makers, hobbyists, and others with relevant instructional or scientific experience.

MATERIALS AND RESOURCES

Assignments may utilize school-provided science materials, classroom supplies, Chromebooks, educational technology, curriculum resources, lesson plans, experiment guides, and other instructional resources where available.

Contractors may use their own instructional methods and materials when appropriate, safe, age-appropriate, lawful, and consistent with the assignment scope and site requirements.

Purchases requiring reimbursement must be approved in writing by Concorde before they are incurred.

Compensation

Compensation varies by assignment and agreed contractor terms. Many opportunities pay $50+ per completed instructional service hour with students.

Contractors may propose their desired compensation rate when applying. When proposing a rate, contractors should consider the overall assignment scope, including anticipated preparation, planning, commute, materials, schedule, and other business considerations.

Concorde may accept the proposed rate, decline the application, or provide a counteroffer based on the budget for the specific assignment.

Unless otherwise approved in writing, compensation is based on completed instructional service hours with students.

Payment for completed services is generally made by direct deposit on the fifteenth day of the month following the month in which services were completed, unless otherwise stated in the accepted assignment terms or required by applicable law.

APPLICATION AND ONBOARDING

Applicants selected to move forward may be invited to create a contractor profile and complete any required onboarding steps.

Applying, interviewing, receiving an invitation to create a profile, creating a profile, or completing onboarding does not guarantee selection, placement, or future assignment opportunities.

Potential assignments are subject to assignment fit, agreed compensation, completion of required onboarding, applicable background-check review, Fair Chance or pre-adverse action procedures where required, site-specific clearance requirements, and final written confirmation from Concorde Education.

Some assignments may require background-check authorization, fingerprinting, agency clearance, site-specific documentation, identification badges, or other compliance steps before services may begin.

Applicants should not provide criminal-history information unless and until requested through the appropriate legally compliant process.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Concorde Education considers contractor applicants without regard to any status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law and is committed to respectful, inclusive, and student-centered programming.

The Department of Nursing at the University of Massachusetts Boston invites applications for a full-time, 12-month Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor A position. Introduction

Join the pioneering AI Foundations Research team at IBM Research and contribute to shaping the future foundations of artificial intelligence. Our group of scientists, engineers, and designers is dedicated to conducting end-to-end research that delivers real-world AI impact through a rigorous, responsible, and open innovation framework. We are the team behind IBM's Granite open-source models, and our work spans multi-modal (vision, speech, language, code) and multi-lingual systems, data quality, data generation, novel model architectures, training recipes, governance and trustworthiness, and programming models for interacting with models. As an intern, you will explore cutting-edge research areas, including new algorithms for training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and inference time scaling, alongside pioneering work in generative computing and generative programming for language, code, and other modalities, all within a collaborative environment that bridges fundamental science and transformative engineering.

Your Role And Responsibilities

As an AI Research Scientist Intern, you will engage in the full research lifecycle to pioneer new advancements in artificial intelligence. Your role will involve identifying core challenges, designing novel prototype solutions, and validating them through rigorous experimentation. You will conduct foundational research in critical areas such as novel training algorithms, efficient fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and inference-time scaling for multi-modal models. Collaborating in small, mentored teams, you will be responsible for shepherding projects from ideation to completion. A key objective is to disseminate significant results through publications in leading conferences and patent applications, contributing to both the academic community and IBM's open innovation initiatives.

Master's Degree

rows.title: Senior Research Associate, Bioengineering
rows.descriptionText:
WHO WE AREODDITY is a consumer tech company that builds and scales digital-first brands to disrupt the offline-dominated beauty and wellness industries. The company serves over 40 million users with its AI-driven online platform, deploying data science to identify consumer needs, and developing solutions in the form of beauty and wellness products. ODDITY owns IL MAKIAGE, SpoiledChild, and medical-grade skincare and telehealth platform METHODIQ. ODDITY LABS is our cutting-edge biotechnology R&D center, powering science-backed product innovation through the discovery and development of new molecules, probiotics, peptides, and other biological modalities. Unlike pharmaceuticals, ingredient innovation in the beauty and wellness industry has remained stagnant for decades. We are deploying patented, proprietary technologies and capabilities, including AI-based molecule discovery and advanced phenotypic databases, to understand the biological mechanisms that drive cellular behavior and develop uniquely efficacious products for beauty and wellness applications. Innovations from the ODDITY LABS will power game-changing products through ODDITY’s current brands, as well as future brands.ODDITY operates with business headquarters in New York City, an R&D center in Tel Aviv, Israel, and a biotechnology lab in Boston. Our culture is fast-paced, innovative, agile, and offers every team member the opportunity to drive a big impact.
THE ROLE
We are seeking a Senior Research Associate to be the hands-on technical anchor for dermatology assay workflows — executing, optimizing, and documenting experiments that support target validation, screening, and translational substantiation. You will work closely with PhD scientists, owning day-to-day bench execution while contributing protocol improvements and training junior staff. This is a high-skill, high-autonomy RA role. Success is measured by reproducible data, assay reliability, and the quality of experimental support you provide to discovery teams.. In this role, you will:Execute and troubleshoot cell-based, biochemical, and phenotypic assays: ELISA, MSD, HTRF/TR-FRET, qPCR, reporter gene assays, viability/cytotoxicity, and flow cytometry.Run in vitro safety packages including genotoxicity, phototoxicity, sensitization, and irritation screens under established SOPs.Support ex vivo human skin explant studies: tissue handling, sample preparation, endpoint readouts, and coordination with analytical partners.Assist with IVPT / Franz diffusion experiments: chamber setup, sampling, permeation sample handling, and LC/MS handoff logistics.Maintain cell lines, reagents, and lab inventory; ensure experiments meet QC and traceability standards.Optimize existing protocols for throughput, reproducibility, and cost efficiency.Draft and maintain SOPs, ELN entries, and raw data packages suitable for internal review and external partner handoff.Perform basic data analysis and figure preparation for scientist-led program updates.Flag experimental anomalies, propose troubleshooting paths, and document deviations.Support an environment that enables a staff of highly skilled and specialized peers to perform biological and computational experiments and promote trust and decision-making.Contribute to promoting a unified office/laboratory culture by organizing and assisting in planning community-building activities.Ensure a clean and safe environment for all laboratory personnel. Enforce and support universal precautions and use of personal protective equipment for all laboratory personnel.
WHO YOU ARE
Bachelor's degree in biological sciences, bioengineering, chemistry, or related field (Master's preferred).4–5 years of hands-on industry or academic laboratory experience in cell/molecular biology.Demonstrated proficiency in multiplex immunoassays, qPCR, and cell-based screening — not solely maintenance-level techniques.Proven expertise with functional assays including reporter cell lines, flow-cytometry, ELISA, cytokine profiling, biochemical assays, and fluorescence imaging.Experience with documentation discipline: ELNs, lab notebooks, SOP adherence, and reproducible experimental records.Ability to work independently on assigned protocols while collaborating in a fast-paced, matrixed R&D environment.Strong organizational skills and attention to detail under concurrent experiment timelines.You have extensive experience with mammalian cell culture, particularly experience with handling primary human cells and immortalized cell lines. Experience with stem cells, iPSC differentiation, various culture substrates, and/or 3D models is ideal.You have prior experience with genetic manipulation of mammalian cells (using either viral vectors, RNAi, CRISPR, etc) and molecular biology techniques, such as nucleic acid preparation, primer design, cloning and Western Blot.Previous experience in processing ex vivo tissue, including histology, transcriptomic profiling, and protein quantification is a plus.You have excellent written and verbal communication skills with experience working with a diverse range of stakeholders.You have a strong attention to detail and are committed to maintaining ODDITY LABS’ high standards and scientific rigor.You are willing to learn new skills as needed to help the team be as successful as it can be.You are an independent problem solver, consistently thinking out of the box and taking the initiative to take the next step without instruction.You are a hard worker with a high level of accountability. You hold yourself to high standards but also expect those around you to as well.
WHAT WE OFFER
Competitive compensation and benefits package.This position will consider and sponsor candidates on a visa (OPT, STEM OPT, H1B, TN).This position is in-office in our Cambridge, Massachusetts office and laboratory.The salary for this position is negotiable and commensurate with experience.Note: We’re currently hiring for many roles! Not the right fit, but interested in another position? Contact us olabs.jobs@oddity.com

Are you looking to make a significant difference by contributing to the field of pulmonary and nasal drug delivery through experimental fluid dynamics and tissue physiology?

Position Overview

We are seeking an ambitious post-doctoral scientist with strong research and communication skills to contribute to highly visible research projects. Experimental fluid dynamics (EFD) in drug delivery uses physical measurements, flow visualizations, and benchtop models to analyze how fluids and therapeutic particles transport, mix, and deposit inside biological systems or testing devices.

The Postdoctoral Scientist - Drug Delivery Experimental Fluid Dynamics sits at the intersection of pulmonary and nasal tissue physiology, inhaled formulation science, and experimental fluid dynamics, supporting the advancement of next-generation inhalation therapies. The successful candidate will work within a multidisciplinary team to characterize device performance through hands-on benchtop and physiologically representative experimental models, using computational tools to complement and extend those experimental findings — contributing directly to formulation design decisions and preclinical-to-clinical translation strategies.

Key Responsibilities

Design and execute in vitro aerosol characterization experiments using experimental fluid dynamics techniques — physical measurements, flow visualization, and benchtop models — on pulmonary and nasal device platforms, assessing droplet size distribution (laser diffraction, cascade impaction), delivered dose, and delivery efficiency.Apply working knowledge of pulmonary and nasal tissue physiology (airway and mucosal anatomy, mucus rheology, and regional structures relevant to deposition and clearance) to design physiologically representative benchtop and ex vivo experimental models, accounting for anatomical variability and its effects on precision and targeting.Apply and interpret existing computational fluid dynamics (CFD) or physiologically based pharmacokinetic/deposition (PBPK/PBPD) models — including uncertainty quantification and sensitivity analysis — to complement experimental data and predict regional aerosol deposition and IVIVC linkages (MMAD, FPF, delivered dose to in vivo or PK/PD endpoints) across patient-representative airway geometries.Collaborate with formulation scientists, device engineers, and translational scientists to integrate experimental and physiological findings into formulation optimization, design space definition, and actionable insights.Communicate findings through internal technical reports, cross-functional presentations, and peer-reviewed publications, and participate in structured mentorship and professional development programming within Lilly’s postdoctoral research community. 


Basic Qualifications

Earned Ph.D. in Biomedical Engineering, Physiology, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Aerosol Science, or a closely related field, conferred within the past 3 years.Demonstrated hands-on experience in experimental fluid dynamics — physical measurements, flow visualization, and benchtop or physiologically representative models of fluid and particle transportExperience designing and executing hands-on experiments and applying characterization techniques (e.g., next-generation impactor [NGI], laser diffraction, DUSA)Working knowledge of tissue physiology and anatomy (ideally airway/mucosal structure, mucus properties, and regional anatomy relevant to aerosol deposition and clearance) and ability to apply literature research toward experiment designStrong publication record commensurate with career stageAbility to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, matrix-based environment.Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1. 


Additional Preferences

Familiarity with computational modeling of aerosol transport and/or deposition (e.g., CFD using ANSYS Fluent/OpenFOAM, or lung deposition models such as MPPD) sufficient to evaluate and apply existing modeling frameworks alongside experimental work.Experience with realistic or idealized airway geometry models (e.g., Weibel, stochastic, or CT-derived anatomical models).Prior industry internship or academic–industry collaborative research experience.Self-directed and highly motivated individual who wants to learn new techniques while continually pursuing research and publication goals.Excellent communicator (oral and written) with presentation experience and a strong publication record; proficient in data analysis and reporting. 


Additional Information

This is a fixed-term role for one year, extendable up to four years, with eligibility to apply for full-time positions upon completion.Position Location: Boston, MATravel Percentage (%): 10

Job Description: 

The Department of Nursing at the University of Massachusetts Boston invites applications for a full-time, 12-month Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor A position. We seek an innovative and student-centered educator who is passionate about undergraduate nursing education and committed to preparing the next generation of nurses to advance health equity and improve health outcomes across diverse communities.

UMass Boston's nursing programs are nationally recognized for their commitment to serving urban populations and addressing health disparities through excellence in education, clinical practice, research, and community engagement. As a public research university with a highly diverse student body, UMass Boston offers a collaborative environment where faculty can make a meaningful impact on student success while contributing to the growth and advancement of the profession. More information is available at www.umb.edu/academics/cnhs.

This position is ideal for a doctoral-prepared nurse educator with expertise in undergraduate nursing curriculum, didactic teaching, and student support. The successful candidate will join a dedicated faculty team committed to academic excellence, innovation, and inclusive student learning.

The teaching load for a 12-month Scholarship of Practice faculty is nine 3 credit courses that are delivered across the academic year.

Key Responsibilities

Teach undergraduate nursing courses using evidence-based and student-centered teaching approaches. Contribute to course and curriculum development, evaluation, and continuous quality improvement initiatives. Support student success through mentoring, advising, remediation, and NCLEX preparation activities using ATI. Utilize innovative instructional technologies and online learning platforms to enhance student engagement. Participate in program assessment, accreditation activities, and ongoing curriculum review. Engage in service activities that support the department, college, and universityContribute to student recruitment, admissions, orientation, progression, and retention efforts. Collaborate effectively with faculty, staff, clinical partners, and students to foster an inclusive learning environment. Attend and actively participate in program, department, college, and university meetings and activities. Maintain professional engagement and contribute to the mission and strategic priorities of the Department of Nursing. 

Required Qualifications

Doctoral degree in Nursing (PhD, DNP, EdD, or equivalent) from an accredited institution.

Current, unencumbered Massachusetts RN license, or eligibility for Massachusetts RN licensure.

Experience teaching nursing in higher education.

Demonstrated expertise in undergraduate nursing education, curriculum development, and student learning assessment.

Strong communication, collaboration, and interpersonal skills.

Commitment to working with diverse student populations and advancing health equity.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience teaching in online and hybrid learning environments.

Record of peer-reviewed, practice-focused scholarship.

Leadership experience within professional nursing organizations.

Demonstrated contributions to professional service, curriculum innovation, or program development.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing and mission-driven nursing department dedicated to educational excellence, community impact, and preparing a diverse nursing workforce equipped to address the healthcare challenges of the future. Candidates who value collaboration, innovation, and student success are encouraged to apply.

Application Instructions:

Submit a letter of interest and curriculum vitae. Finalists will need to supply graduate transcripts and names and contact information of at least three references.

Review of applications will continue until the positions are filled.

UMass Boston expects to pay within an approximate range between $104,700 and $135,000 for this position.

The specific pay for this position will be determined by the University based on the consideration of all relevant factors when and if it decides to extend an offer of employment.

UMass Boston is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, we will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations for the hiring process. If reasonable accommodation is needed, please contact HR@umb.edu or 617-287-5150.

rows.title: Science Teaching Opportunities
rows.descriptionText:
POTENTIAL INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR INSTRUCTIONAL ASSIGNMENTS

Program: Science Instructor Opportunities

Location: On-site at partner schools; varies by assignment

Teaching Mode: In Person

Grade Levels: Elementary, Middle, and High School; varies by assignment

Schedule: Typically 1–4 instructional service hours per week after school

Program Length: Commonly approximately 10 weeks per assignment

Start Dates: Opportunities become available throughout the school year

Compensation: Typical compensation of $50+ per completed instructional service hour, depending on assignment scope, experience, location, schedule, and agreed compensation

About The Opportunity

Concorde Education is seeking independent instructional contractors to provide engaging, hands-on science enrichment services for K–12 students.

This is a potential independent contractor assignment, not an employee position. Contractors may choose whether to apply for, accept, decline, or ignore available opportunities.

Assignments vary by school, grade level, schedule, curriculum, available materials, available technology, and program objectives.

Concorde may provide curriculum guidance, lesson-plan suggestions, activity ideas, instructional resources, or program objectives. Contractors may use their professional judgment to adapt instruction within the assignment scope and applicable site requirements.

ASSIGNMENT SCOPE

Depending On The Accepted Assignment, Contractors May

 Plan and facilitate engaging, age-appropriate science enrichment sessions; Introduce students to scientific concepts through safe, hands-on experiments, demonstrations, investigations, and project-based learning; Adapt activities based on student experience levels, site requirements, available materials, and program objectives; Guide students through observation, experimentation, data collection, critical thinking, and scientific inquiry, where applicable; Maintain a safe, respectful, inclusive, and age-appropriate learning environment; Communicate assignment-related needs or significant concerns with Concorde and school staff, as appropriate; Complete a brief session completion form after each scheduled session; and Follow applicable site safety, visitor, technology, emergency, and student-protection procedures.

EXAMPLE PROGRAM TOPICS

Assignments May Include Topics Such As

 Everyday chemistry using safe household materials; States of matter and simple chemical reactions; Kitchen science and food chemistry; Cleaning science and how soaps and surfactants work; Simple machines, force, and motion; Engineering and design challenges using common household materials; Environmental science, recycling, ecosystems, energy, and sustainability; Observation, experimentation, measurement, and the scientific method; and Scientific reasoning, problem-solving, and STEM exploration.

Specific content, curriculum requirements, experiments, and instructional resources vary by assignment.

Qualifications

Preferred qualifications include:

 At least 60 college credits, where required by the applicable assignment or site; Experience teaching, tutoring, coaching, mentoring, or leading activities with school-age students; Comfort explaining age-appropriate science concepts through engaging, hands-on instruction; Strong communication, organization, and classroom facilitation skills; Availability to provide services for the accepted assignment schedule and communicate schedule issues as soon as reasonably practicable; and Familiarity with classroom technology, Chromebooks, web-based educational platforms, or related instructional tools.

Preferred backgrounds may include educators, science teachers, STEM professionals, college or graduate students studying science or education, tutors, camp counselors, engineers, healthcare professionals, makers, hobbyists, and others with relevant instructional or scientific experience.

MATERIALS AND RESOURCES

Assignments may utilize school-provided science materials, classroom supplies, Chromebooks, educational technology, curriculum resources, lesson plans, experiment guides, and other instructional resources where available.

Contractors may use their own instructional methods and materials when appropriate, safe, age-appropriate, lawful, and consistent with the assignment scope and site requirements.

Purchases requiring reimbursement must be approved in writing by Concorde before they are incurred.

Compensation

Compensation varies by assignment and agreed contractor terms. Many opportunities pay $50+ per completed instructional service hour with students.

Contractors may propose their desired compensation rate when applying. When proposing a rate, contractors should consider the overall assignment scope, including anticipated preparation, planning, commute, materials, schedule, and other business considerations.

Concorde may accept the proposed rate, decline the application, or provide a counteroffer based on the budget for the specific assignment.

Unless otherwise approved in writing, compensation is based on completed instructional service hours with students.

Payment for completed services is generally made by direct deposit on the fifteenth day of the month following the month in which services were completed, unless otherwise stated in the accepted assignment terms or required by applicable law.

APPLICATION AND ONBOARDING

Applicants selected to move forward may be invited to create a contractor profile and complete any required onboarding steps.

Applying, interviewing, receiving an invitation to create a profile, creating a profile, or completing onboarding does not guarantee selection, placement, or future assignment opportunities.

Potential assignments are subject to assignment fit, agreed compensation, completion of required onboarding, applicable background-check review, Fair Chance or pre-adverse action procedures where required, site-specific clearance requirements, and final written confirmation from Concorde Education.

Some assignments may require background-check authorization, fingerprinting, agency clearance, site-specific documentation, identification badges, or other compliance steps before services may begin.

Applicants should not provide criminal-history information unless and until requested through the appropriate legally compliant process.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Concorde Education considers contractor applicants without regard to any status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law and is committed to respectful, inclusive, and student-centered programming.

TERADYNE, where experience meets innovation and driving excellence in every connection. We are fueled by creativity and diversity of thought and in our workforce. Our employees are supported to innovate and learn something new every day.

We cultivate a culture of inclusion for all employees that respects their individual strengths, views, and experiences. We believe that our differences enable us to be a better team – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better business results.

The Factory Applications group is seeking a motivated, self-driven engineer to support our Silicon Photonics product team. Develop knowledge and expertise on semiconductor device testing. rows.descriptionText:
Introduction

Join the pioneering AI Foundations Research team at IBM Research and contribute to shaping the future foundations of artificial intelligence. Our group of scientists, engineers, and designers is dedicated to conducting end-to-end research that delivers real-world AI impact through a rigorous, responsible, and open innovation framework. We are the team behind IBM's Granite open-source models, and our work spans multi-modal (vision, speech, language, code) and multi-lingual systems, data quality, data generation, novel model architectures, training recipes, governance and trustworthiness, and programming models for interacting with models. As an intern, you will explore cutting-edge research areas, including new algorithms for training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and inference time scaling, alongside pioneering work in generative computing and generative programming for language, code, and other modalities, all within a collaborative environment that bridges fundamental science and transformative engineering.

Your Role And Responsibilities

As an AI Research Scientist Intern, you will engage in the full research lifecycle to pioneer new advancements in artificial intelligence. Your role will involve identifying core challenges, designing novel prototype solutions, and validating them through rigorous experimentation. You will conduct foundational research in critical areas such as novel training algorithms, efficient fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and inference-time scaling for multi-modal models. Collaborating in small, mentored teams, you will be responsible for shepherding projects from ideation to completion. A key objective is to disseminate significant results through publications in leading conferences and patent applications, contributing to both the academic community and IBM's open innovation initiatives.

Master's Degree

Research Experience with Modern ML: Hands-on experience with and a deep theoretical understanding of Large Language Models (LLMs), Vision-Language Models (VLMs), and Transformer-based architectures.Strong Programming & Prototyping Skills: Proficiency in Python for rapid prototyping, experimental setup, and implementing large-scale machine learning systems.Rigorous Analytical & Problem-Solving Abilities: Demonstrated strength in quantitative analysis, designing experiments, and deconstructing complex research problems.Proven Research & Communication Skills: A track record of innovation (evidenced by peer-reviewed publications or strong preprints) and the ability to clearly articulate complex technical concepts in both writing and presentations.Collaborative Research Mindset: A team-oriented approach with a commitment to rigorous, reproducible, and well-documented research practices.

Preferred Technical And Professional Experience

Research Excellence: Strong publication record in top-tier conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, AAAI).Technical Proficiency: Advanced expertise in ML frameworks (PyTorch) and full-cycle development of algorithms and systems.Specialized Skills: Hands-on experience with generative AI (LLMs) and multimodal models, from training to testing.Communication: Demonstrated ability to present complex research and build high-impact technical demonstrations.

You hold yourself to high standards but also expect those around you to as well.
WHAT WE OFFER
Competitive compensation and benefits package.This position will consider and sponsor candidates on a visa (OPT, STEM OPT, H1B, TN).This position is in-office in our Cambridge, Massachusetts office and laboratory.The salary for this position is negotiable and commensurate with experience.Note: We’re currently hiring for many roles! rows.title: Data Analyst Role
rows.descriptionText:
Description

The work

Data Analysts make operational data answerable. They work with stakeholders to define measures, acquire and reconcile data, investigate discrepancies, and turn recurring questions into analyses, reports, semantic models, and dashboards that people can use.

The daily craft combines SQL, spreadsheets, scripting, and business intelligence tools with careful domain reasoning. Data Analysts profile and clean data, define calculations, identify trends and exceptions, validate results against source systems, and present the finding in language suited to the decision.

What You'll Build

 Recurring reports and dashboards with documented measures, refresh schedules, filters, alerts, and access controls. Clean analytical datasets and semantic models that reconcile source fields, business definitions, relationships, and calculation logic. Queries, scripts, and repeatable workflows that replace manual reporting and make transformations easier to test and review. Variance, trend, cohort, performance, financial, program, or operational analyses that identify what changed and where to investigate. Data-quality checks, reconciliation reports, issue logs, and documentation that establish where a number came from and whether it is fit for use.

Who You Are

You are precise with numbers and curious about what sits behind them. An unexplained variance is an invitation to trace definitions, filters, timing, and source records until the result makes sense.

You can shift between a stakeholder's question and the data needed to answer it. You communicate clearly, design for the people who will use the analysis, and distinguish a useful operational conclusion from a claim the data cannot support.

What You Bring

 Practical skill in querying, cleaning, joining, aggregating, and validating data with SQL, spreadsheets, scripting, or comparable analytical tools. Experience defining measures, documenting business rules, reconciling sources, and building reports or dashboards that refresh reliably. Working knowledge of descriptive statistics, trend analysis, outlier investigation, data modeling, and visualization selection. Habits that make analysis reproducible, including version control where appropriate, documented transformations, quality checks, and peer review. The ability to present findings, assumptions, limitations, and recommended follow-up to technical and nontechnical audiences.

About OPEN Data Jobs

OPEN Data Jobs connects AI, data, and software professionals with critical roles, primarily in the federal sector. Registering with ODJ can put your profile in view for multiple positions across several clients.

Job Summary

NORC at the University of Chicago is seeking a qualified Data Analyst I or II (we are open to hiring at either level) to join the Health Sciences Department to support hospital discharge data processing across states and harmonizing and packaging files into a uniform format. At NORC, Data Analysts are early career team members who train and work with our senior Research Scientists, Statisticians, and Data Scientists to perform tasks such as data processing, quality assurance, analysis, and dissemination.

As part of their data processing responsibilities, Data Analysts import, clean, standardize, transform, and validate data sets. They also research and document data procedures and support the investigation of data problems. They may identify, analyze, and interpret trends or patterns in data sets, and help prepare data presentations and reports, including developing charts, graphs, and tables. In addition, the Data Analyst may assist in data collection and harmonization from primary or secondary data sources (e.g., administrative records, commercial data, social media data), preparing data files for delivery, and the maintenance of databases, data systems, and their relevant metadata/dictionaries. The Data Analyst is expected to work collaboratively in a team environment.

For this role, proficiency in SAS is a requirement. Experience with R or Python is welcome but not essential. Prior work with healthcare or administrative claims data is preferred, and strong documentation practices are important.

Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Location : This is a hybrid role based in either our Chicago Loop or downtown DC office, with a minimum of six days per month in the office. Exceptional remote candidates may be considered as well.

DEPARTMENT: Health Science Research

NORC’s Health Sciences staff produce rich data on social priorities including child development and healthy aging, the uses of electronic clinical data in research, and the applications and effectiveness of health information technology.

The Health Sciences team is versatile and experienced in data acquisition, management, technical assistance, and analysis; the use of information technology in health care; and numerous data collection methods. Our track record of leadership and innovation includes the design and management of large-scale surveys, including extensive experience collecting biomeasures.

Responsibilities

 Collaborate with researchers, statisticians, data scientists, technology experts, and subject matter experts to implement and improve data management, processing, and analysis activities.  Develop programs and scripts for data cleaning, integration, transformation, and harmonization, as well as data quality checks and validation  Support and enhance applications and databases already built for various research needs and produce data documentation and dictionaries.  Contribute to documentation, reports, and presentations through writing sections, creating basic analytic summaries, and developing tables and graphics.  Apply AI tools to help improve efficiency.  Perform other duties as assigned. 

Required Skills

 Bachelor’s degree in one of the following fields: quantitative social sciences, public health, statistics, biostatistics, health informatics, math, data science, or computer science, or related field required. Please include a Resume and Cover Letter when applying. Candidates should be prepared to provide professional references upon request.

Salary And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $62,000 – $77,000.
