rows.title: Generative AI Engineer Role
rows.descriptionText:
Description

The work

Generative AI Engineers build production applications around foundation models and large language models. They turn model capabilities into tools for search, drafting, summarization, information extraction, multimodal work, and guided action, with the controls and evidence needed to understand how those tools behave.

The role concentrates on application and context engineering. Generative AI Engineers connect models to authoritative knowledge, tools, and workflows; design prompts and structured outputs; evaluate quality, grounding, safety, security, latency, and cost; and monitor the application after release. They treat fluent output as something to test, not proof that the system is correct.

What You'll Build

 Grounded assistants and knowledge applications with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), hybrid or vector search, citations, metadata filtering, and source-level access controls. Drafting, summarization, classification, extraction, and transformation services exposed through user interfaces or APIs. Agents and multistep workflows with defined tool schemas, constrained permissions, approval gates, memory boundaries, replay, and exception handling. Evaluation systems with curated test cases, task-specific rubrics, retrieval measures, grounding checks, safety and security tests, and regression thresholds. Operational pipelines for versioning prompts and configurations, comparing models, tracing execution, monitoring quality and cost, collecting feedback, and responding to incidents.

Who You Are

You are an application engineer who can work with fast-moving model capabilities without chasing every new release. You choose architectures by evidence, make uncertainty visible, and separate a convincing demonstration from a dependable service.

You think in complete workflows: sources, context, models, tools, permissions, people, and failure paths. You collaborate with domain experts, data and software engineers, security and privacy specialists, and accountable owners to decide where generation helps and where deterministic methods or human judgment should remain in control.

What You Bring

 A strong application-engineering foundation, including programming, APIs, testing, version control, service integration, and production debugging. Practical experience with foundation-model integration, prompt and context design, structured outputs, model selection, and failure analysis. Working knowledge of retrieval systems, embeddings, search, knowledge stores, document ingestion, and data-access controls. Evaluation discipline across answer quality, retrieval relevance, grounding, safety, security, latency, cost, and user outcomes. The judgment to constrain tools and agents, design human-review paths, document limitations, and respond when production behavior changes.

Activities will include analyzing emerging AI methodologies, contributing to frameworks that guide responsible AI adoption in a regulatory environment, and documenting insights that can inform Agency-wide AI governance and implementation efforts. You will apply machine learning methods and applied AI tools, including experience with large language models (LLMs) - spanning open-source models, LLM architecture, prompt design, and agentic AI frameworks - to help evaluate and advance responsible AI integration across the Agency.

Project 3: Pilot and Proof-of-Concept Applications

You will collaborate with FDA staff to design and develop pilot applications and proof-of-concept tools. These activities will aim at investigating how automation, machine learning, and advanced analytics can improve internal processes, streamline analytical workflows, and enhance the efficiency of regulatory research and operations. You will apply hands-on programming skills in R and Python, acting within server-side development environments such as RStudio, JupyterLab, and RSConnect, and will document development decisions and contribute to knowledge-sharing within the team.

Project 4: Data Visualization

You will participate in the development of interactive dashboards and visual analytics tools. Activities will include designing visualizations that enable FDA staff to efficiently explore and communicate complex datasets, and contributing to the adoption of visualization best practices in support of regulatory and public health decision-making. You will apply hands-on skills using frameworks such as Plotly, Dash, and R Shiny to translate complex data into clear, actionable visual analytics and dashboards.

Mentored research experiences with FDA subject matter experts in data science, AI, public health policy, and regulatory science.Participation in relevant training programs, seminars, and workshops on emerging technologies, including AI methodologies and responsible use of large language models (LLMs).Skill development in scientific and technical writing, data engineering, machine learning, and data visualization.Exposure to cross-agency collaborations and the opportunity to learn from interdisciplinary teams spanning epidemiology, economics, and health policy.Attendance at high-level policy and planning meetings with the office director, staff, and FDA senior leadership.

This fellowship will provide you with a strong foundation for a career in regulatory science, applied data science, or public health policy. By contributing to high-impact research and tool development projects, you will build a robust portfolio of technical, analytical, and collaborative skills. Engagement with FDA's regulatory science network and exposure to real-world policy and operational challenges will position you as a competitive candidate for advanced roles in government, academia, or the private sector.

rows.title: AI Engineer Role
rows.descriptionText:
Description

The work

AI Engineers build and operate systems that turn data, documents, models, and AI services into useful applications and workflows. The work runs from understanding the problem and preparing inputs through model or service selection, system design, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, incident response, and continuous improvement.

This is systems engineering around AI behavior. AI Engineers connect data pipelines, models, APIs, user experiences, business rules, and human-review paths, then test the complete system under conditions that reflect how people will use it. They make limitations visible and match security, traceability, and oversight to the consequences of the work.

What You'll Build

Document and content pipelines that apply OCR, parse layouts, extract and validate information, preserve provenance, and make authoritative content usable downstream.Predictive, classification, recommendation, natural language, computer vision, or decision-support services that combine custom models, pretrained models, externally provided AI services, and deterministic software.Search and knowledge applications that use retrieval, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), controlled source access, and traceable references.Workflow and agent-based systems with scoped tools, permission boundaries, approval paths, exception handling, and audit trails where agentic patterns fit the problem.Evaluation and operations capabilities that version, test, release, trace, monitor, diagnose, and roll back models, prompts, configurations, retrieval indexes, and supporting software.

Who You Are

You see the model as one part of a larger system. You can move between user needs, data, software, model behavior, and production operations without losing sight of the outcome, and you choose the simplest approach that meets the need.

You test assumptions against evidence, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and work comfortably with domain experts, users, data engineers, data scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, security specialists, governance teams, and operations teams. You know when to build, when to integrate, when to escalate, and when AI is not the right answer.

What You Bring

A working foundation in software engineering, including programming, APIs, testing, version control, and the design of services or applications.Practical experience with structured or unstructured data, including preparation, validation, metadata, access controls, quality, and traceability.Applied understanding of AI and machine learning, including model or service selection, evaluation design, error analysis, and clear communication of limitations.Experience contributing to production reliability through deployment discipline, observability, performance and cost management, security, incident response, or related operational practices.The judgment to match evaluation, documentation, safeguards, and human oversight to the context and consequences of the system.

What Openings May Require

An opening may emphasize document intelligence, conventional ML, generative AI, RAG, agents, computer vision, AI platforms, machine learning operations (MLOps), generative AI operations, evaluation, security, governance, or a particular mission domain.

Specific openings may name programming languages, cloud environments, model providers, ML frameworks, document-processing tools, search or vector platforms, workflow and agent frameworks, data stores, container and deployment platforms, observability systems, or regulated-development practices. OPEN Data Jobs will identify the required and preferred capabilities with each opening.

The Landolt Mission team is responsible for developing and executing a NASA space-based mission through coordinated work across science, payload, spacecraft bus, software, systems engineering, integration and test, mission assurance, and project management functions. The unit provides an interdisciplinary research and training environment for faculty, postdoctoral researchers, engineers, staff, and students working collaboratively with federal, academic, commercial, and other external partners.

The Mason Space Center is an academic center at George Mason University established to provide administrative, facilities, academic, and outreach infrastructure supporting space mission activities at GMU.

This position is sponsored by the NASA Landolt mission and Mason Space Center (MSC). The Landolt project will develop and operate a small satellite with calibrated light sources onboard to simulate a star and use ground telescopes to transfer absolute brightness calibration to selected real stars. This grant-funded postdoctoral position is intended to support the Landolt mission through scientific, technical, and programmatic contributions. rows.title: Machine Learning Engineer Role
rows.descriptionText:
Description

The work

Machine Learning Engineers make machine learning and AI models reproducible, deployable, scalable, and supportable. They build the path from training data and experimentation to a versioned model service that can be released, monitored, retrained, and retired without guesswork.

The role centers on the model lifecycle and the platform beneath it. Machine Learning Engineers automate training and validation, manage features and model artifacts, optimize inference, implement machine learning operations (MLOps), and watch for changes in data, behavior, performance, reliability, and cost. They create the shared tooling that lets data scientists and application engineers move models into production safely.

What You'll Build

 Reproducible training, validation, tuning, and retraining pipelines with versioned data, code, parameters, environments, and model artifacts. Model-serving systems and APIs designed for appropriate latency, throughput, availability, scaling, and rollback. Feature pipelines, feature stores, model registries, lineage records, approval workflows, and automated release controls. Monitoring and alerting for data quality, drift, model performance, fairness, infrastructure health, latency, and cost. Reusable libraries, templates, environments, and delivery pipelines that give data scientists a tested path from experiment to production.

Who You Are

You are comfortable at the seam between modeling and software engineering. You can inspect a model, harden a pipeline, diagnose a production failure, and improve the platform so the same class of problem is easier to prevent next time.

You value repeatability over heroics. You work closely with data scientists on model behavior, data engineers on reliable inputs, AI Engineers on application integration, and platform and security teams on the environment in which the model runs.

What You Bring

 Strong programming and software-engineering practice, including testing, version control, packaging, automation, and production debugging. Working knowledge of model development, evaluation metrics, feature engineering, data splitting, tuning, and the limits of different modeling approaches. Experience with training and inference pipelines, containers, cloud or on-premises compute, artifact management, and automated deployment. Practical MLOps experience with model registries, lineage, reproducibility, monitoring, drift analysis, retraining, release controls, and rollback. The ability to balance model quality with reliability, interpretability, security, privacy, latency, throughput, and cost.

rows.title: Data Scientist Role
rows.descriptionText:
Description

The work

Data Scientists turn difficult questions and complex data into evidence. They work with stakeholders to define what should be measured, determine whether the available data can support the question, select appropriate statistical or machine learning methods, and explain what the results do and do not establish.

The work runs from exploratory analysis through model development, validation, interpretation, and communication. Data Scientists examine data quality and bias, test assumptions, quantify uncertainty, compare alternatives, document methods, and make analyses reproducible. When a model will be used repeatedly, they help define how its performance should be assessed over time.

What You'll Build

 Forecasting, classification, risk, anomaly-detection, segmentation, causal, simulation, or optimization models matched to the question and available evidence. Exploratory analyses that reveal distributions, relationships, outliers, missingness, and limits in the data before formal modeling begins. Experimental or quasi-experimental designs, sampling plans, measurement strategies, and evaluation frameworks. Reproducible analytical pipelines, notebooks, code, data documentation, model cards, and validation reports that allow others to follow the work. Decision briefings and analytical products that communicate results, uncertainty, assumptions, limitations, and appropriate uses to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Who You Are

You are rigorous about methods and candid about uncertainty. You would rather narrow a claim than overstate the evidence, and you are willing to report a null or inconvenient result when that is what the analysis supports.

You are curious about the domain, not only the dataset. You work with subject-matter experts, analysts, engineers, and decision-makers to frame the right question, challenge assumptions, and turn technical results into conclusions people can use responsibly.

What You Bring

 A working foundation in statistics, probability, research design, ML, optimization, or another quantitative discipline relevant to the opening. Ability to prepare, explore, and analyze data using tools such as Python, R, or SQL, with attention to quality and provenance. Experience selecting methods, validating assumptions, comparing models, investigating errors, and interpreting results in context. Reproducible practice through documented code, version control, peer review, traceable data transformations, and clear analytical records. The communication judgment to explain uncertainty, bias, limitations, and appropriate use without hiding the central finding.

rows.title: Research Scientist-Arctic Acoustics Modeling and field Operations
rows.descriptionText:
We are seeking a highly adaptable and self-directed Signal Processing Scientist to join our dynamic research and development team. This role is designed for a creative, practical problem-solver who thrives on breadth and variety, rather than being confined to a single narrow project.

In this role, you will bridge the gap between advanced academic research and real-world operational impact. You will leverage your creative instincts and deep technical expertise to translate complex mathematical models—specifically in universal spectral estimation and array processing—into efficient, testable code applied to CUI and classified datasets. We offer a highly collaborative environment that values innovative approaches, rapid prototyping, and autonomy to critically evaluate and dictate technical solutions.

Work Schedule: M – F 8 AM – 5 PM EST

Essential Responsibilities: 

Acoustic Modeling & Prediction: Utilize numerical acoustic propagation models to generate statistical predictions of transmission loss and ambient sound in realistic Arctic environments. Data Integration & Analysis: Incorporate complex environmental datasets—including satellite observations, oceanographic forecasts, and field observations—into numerical simulations to ensure accurate real-world modeling. Model Validation: Test and validate physical models for transmission loss and ambient sound predictions against empirical acoustic recordings gathered in under-ice environments. Field Operations & Logistics: Support experimental preparation and on-ice Arctic field work. This encompasses testing observing equipment in a laboratory setting, assisting with experiment planning, and managing field logistics. Scientific Communication: Author technical reports, document experimental methodologies, and present complex scientific findings clearly to internal teams and external stakeholders. Travel & Deployment: Participate in occasional field travel to collect data in Arctic environments (travel is not expected to exceed 3–4 weeks per year). 

Work Environment, Physical Demands, and Mental Demands: Field work is required.

Minimum Requirements (Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities):

I. Knowledge

Scientific Programming: Extensive experience utilizing programming languages such as Fortran, C++, Python, or Matlab for modeling and data analysis. Numerical Simulations: Deep understanding of numerical simulations and mathematical methods applied to wave propagation. Observational Equipment: Familiarity with the mechanics, deployment, and operation of acoustics and/or ocean science observing equipment. Signal Processing: Strong foundational knowledge in signal processing techniques as applied to experimental physics or oceanography. 

II. Skills

Experimental Data Analysis: Proven skill in reducing, processing, and analyzing complex, noisy datasets (e.g., under-ice acoustic recordings) to extract actionable scientific insights. Technical Writing: Strong scientific writing skills, with the ability to document algorithms, physical models, and field results clearly for both peer-reviewed and operational audiences. Equipment Troubleshooting: Hands-on capability to set up, calibrate, and troubleshoot sensitive observational equipment in a lab environment prior to field deployment. 

III. Abilities

Adaptability & Field Readiness: Ability to successfully operate and collect data in remote, harsh, or austere environments (specifically Arctic on-ice conditions) for short durations (3-4 weeks/year). Autonomy & Initiative: Self-directed and capable of driving both computational and logistical tasks forward with minimal supervision. Collaboration: Ability to work seamlessly across multidisciplinary teams, bridging the gap between theoretical modelers and physical field operators. Precision: Highly detail-oriented, ensuring rigorous accuracy in both numerical code execution and physical equipment calibration. 

Security Clearance Required: Candidates without a secret clearance can be considered; they will be upgraded to secret once they receive their interim clearance. We will need to start once security paperwork is in the DOW database and the SF86 has been verified.

 Minimum Education: Education: Degree in Oceanography, Physics, Acoustics, Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related scientific discipline. (Specify required degree level here, e.g., M.S. or Ph.D., or B.S. with equivalent experience). Domain Experience: Demonstrated applied experience in experimental data analysis, wave propagation simulations, and acoustics. Unique Backgrounds: Candidates who possess a blend of rigorous computational modeling experience combined with practical, hands-on mechanical troubleshooting or field-expedition experience are highly encouraged to apply. 

Minimum Years of Experience: 0-2 Ph.D., 2-4, Masters, 3-5 BS.

rows.title: Machine Learning Engineer Role
rows.descriptionText:
Description

The work

Machine Learning Engineers make machine learning and AI models reproducible, deployable, scalable, and supportable. They build the path from training data and experimentation to a versioned model service that can be released, monitored, retrained, and retired without guesswork.

The role centers on the model lifecycle and the platform beneath it. Machine Learning Engineers automate training and validation, manage features and model artifacts, optimize inference, implement machine learning operations (MLOps), and watch for changes in data, behavior, performance, reliability, and cost. They create the shared tooling that lets data scientists and application engineers move models into production safely.

What You'll Build

 Reproducible training, validation, tuning, and retraining pipelines with versioned data, code, parameters, environments, and model artifacts. Model-serving systems and APIs designed for appropriate latency, throughput, availability, scaling, and rollback. Feature pipelines, feature stores, model registries, lineage records, approval workflows, and automated release controls. Monitoring and alerting for data quality, drift, model performance, fairness, infrastructure health, latency, and cost. Reusable libraries, templates, environments, and delivery pipelines that give data scientists a tested path from experiment to production.

Who You Are

You are comfortable at the seam between modeling and software engineering. You can inspect a model, harden a pipeline, diagnose a production failure, and improve the platform so the same class of problem is easier to prevent next time.

You value repeatability over heroics. You work closely with data scientists on model behavior, data engineers on reliable inputs, AI Engineers on application integration, and platform and security teams on the environment in which the model runs.

What You Bring

 Strong programming and software-engineering practice, including testing, version control, packaging, automation, and production debugging. Working knowledge of model development, evaluation metrics, feature engineering, data splitting, tuning, and the limits of different modeling approaches. Experience with training and inference pipelines, containers, cloud or on-premises compute, artifact management, and automated deployment. Practical MLOps experience with model registries, lineage, reproducibility, monitoring, drift analysis, retraining, release controls, and rollback. The ability to balance model quality with reliability, interpretability, security, privacy, latency, throughput, and cost.

rows.title: AI Engineer Role
rows.descriptionText:
Description

The work

AI Engineers build and operate systems that turn data, documents, models, and AI services into useful applications and workflows. The work runs from understanding the problem and preparing inputs through model or service selection, system design, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, incident response, and continuous improvement.

This is systems engineering around AI behavior. AI Engineers connect data pipelines, models, APIs, user experiences, business rules, and human-review paths, then test the complete system under conditions that reflect how people will use it. They make limitations visible and match security, traceability, and oversight to the consequences of the work.

What You'll Build

Document and content pipelines that apply OCR, parse layouts, extract and validate information, preserve provenance, and make authoritative content usable downstream.Predictive, classification, recommendation, natural language, computer vision, or decision-support services that combine custom models, pretrained models, externally provided AI services, and deterministic software.Search and knowledge applications that use retrieval, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), controlled source access, and traceable references.Workflow and agent-based systems with scoped tools, permission boundaries, approval paths, exception handling, and audit trails where agentic patterns fit the problem.Evaluation and operations capabilities that version, test, release, trace, monitor, diagnose, and roll back models, prompts, configurations, retrieval indexes, and supporting software.

Who You Are

You see the model as one part of a larger system. You can move between user needs, data, software, model behavior, and production operations without losing sight of the outcome, and you choose the simplest approach that meets the need.

You test assumptions against evidence, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and work comfortably with domain experts, users, data engineers, data scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, security specialists, governance teams, and operations teams. You know when to build, when to integrate, when to escalate, and when AI is not the right answer.

What You Bring

A working foundation in software engineering, including programming, APIs, testing, version control, and the design of services or applications.Practical experience with structured or unstructured data, including preparation, validation, metadata, access controls, quality, and traceability.Applied understanding of AI and machine learning, including model or service selection, evaluation design, error analysis, and clear communication of limitations.Experience contributing to production reliability through deployment discipline, observability, performance and cost management, security, incident response, or related operational practices.The judgment to match evaluation, documentation, safeguards, and human oversight to the context and consequences of the system.

What Openings May Require

An opening may emphasize document intelligence, conventional ML, generative AI, RAG, agents, computer vision, AI platforms, machine learning operations (MLOps), generative AI operations, evaluation, security, governance, or a particular mission domain.

Specific openings may name programming languages, cloud environments, model providers, ML frameworks, document-processing tools, search or vector platforms, workflow and agent frameworks, data stores, container and deployment platforms, observability systems, or regulated-development practices. rows.title: Generative AI Engineer Role
rows.descriptionText:
Description

The work

Generative AI Engineers build production applications around foundation models and large language models. They turn model capabilities into tools for search, drafting, summarization, information extraction, multimodal work, and guided action, with the controls and evidence needed to understand how those tools behave.

The role concentrates on application and context engineering. Generative AI Engineers connect models to authoritative knowledge, tools, and workflows; design prompts and structured outputs; evaluate quality, grounding, safety, security, latency, and cost; and monitor the application after release. They treat fluent output as something to test, not proof that the system is correct.

What You'll Build

 Grounded assistants and knowledge applications with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), hybrid or vector search, citations, metadata filtering, and source-level access controls. Drafting, summarization, classification, extraction, and transformation services exposed through user interfaces or APIs. Agents and multistep workflows with defined tool schemas, constrained permissions, approval gates, memory boundaries, replay, and exception handling. Evaluation systems with curated test cases, task-specific rubrics, retrieval measures, grounding checks, safety and security tests, and regression thresholds. Operational pipelines for versioning prompts and configurations, comparing models, tracing execution, monitoring quality and cost, collecting feedback, and responding to incidents.

Who You Are

You are an application engineer who can work with fast-moving model capabilities without chasing every new release. You choose architectures by evidence, make uncertainty visible, and separate a convincing demonstration from a dependable service.

You think in complete workflows: sources, context, models, tools, permissions, people, and failure paths. You collaborate with domain experts, data and software engineers, security and privacy specialists, and accountable owners to decide where generation helps and where deterministic methods or human judgment should remain in control.

What You Bring

 A strong application-engineering foundation, including programming, APIs, testing, version control, service integration, and production debugging. Practical experience with foundation-model integration, prompt and context design, structured outputs, model selection, and failure analysis. Working knowledge of retrieval systems, embeddings, search, knowledge stores, document ingestion, and data-access controls. Evaluation discipline across answer quality, retrieval relevance, grounding, safety, security, latency, cost, and user outcomes. The judgment to constrain tools and agents, design human-review paths, document limitations, and respond when production behavior changes.

Specific openings may name a model provider, cloud platform, vector or search service, agent framework, observability stack, programming language, model-evaluation approach, content-safety service, or security and governance framework. rows.title: AI Engineer Role
rows.descriptionText:
Description

The work

AI Engineers build and operate systems that turn data, documents, models, and AI services into useful applications and workflows. The work runs from understanding the problem and preparing inputs through model or service selection, system design, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, incident response, and continuous improvement.

This is systems engineering around AI behavior. AI Engineers connect data pipelines, models, APIs, user experiences, business rules, and human-review paths, then test the complete system under conditions that reflect how people will use it. They make limitations visible and match security, traceability, and oversight to the consequences of the work.

What You'll Build

Document and content pipelines that apply OCR, parse layouts, extract and validate information, preserve provenance, and make authoritative content usable downstream.Predictive, classification, recommendation, natural language, computer vision, or decision-support services that combine custom models, pretrained models, externally provided AI services, and deterministic software.Search and knowledge applications that use retrieval, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), controlled source access, and traceable references.Workflow and agent-based systems with scoped tools, permission boundaries, approval paths, exception handling, and audit trails where agentic patterns fit the problem.Evaluation and operations capabilities that version, test, release, trace, monitor, diagnose, and roll back models, prompts, configurations, retrieval indexes, and supporting software.

Who You Are

You see the model as one part of a larger system. You can move between user needs, data, software, model behavior, and production operations without losing sight of the outcome, and you choose the simplest approach that meets the need.

You test assumptions against evidence, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and work comfortably with domain experts, users, data engineers, data scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, security specialists, governance teams, and operations teams. You know when to build, when to integrate, when to escalate, and when AI is not the right answer.

What You Bring

A working foundation in software engineering, including programming, APIs, testing, version control, and the design of services or applications.Practical experience with structured or unstructured data, including preparation, validation, metadata, access controls, quality, and traceability.Applied understanding of AI and machine learning, including model or service selection, evaluation design, error analysis, and clear communication of limitations.Experience contributing to production reliability through deployment discipline, observability, performance and cost management, security, incident response, or related operational practices.The judgment to match evaluation, documentation, safeguards, and human oversight to the context and consequences of the system.

What Openings May Require

An opening may emphasize document intelligence, conventional ML, generative AI, RAG, agents, computer vision, AI platforms, machine learning operations (MLOps), generative AI operations, evaluation, security, governance, or a particular mission domain.

Specific openings may name programming languages, cloud environments, model providers, ML frameworks, document-processing tools, search or vector platforms, workflow and agent frameworks, data stores, container and deployment platforms, observability systems, or regulated-development practices. OPEN Data Jobs will identify the required and preferred capabilities with each opening.

Compensation And Benefits

Compensation, benefits, work location, and employment terms are set for each specific opening and will be stated with that opening.

Develop reports and whitepapers that evaluate solution alternatives based on impact, cost, technical feasibility, and alignment with strategic goals. Job Title: Customer Development Manager – Walmart (L'Oréal Dermatological Beauty)

Division: L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty (LDB)

Reports To: VP Commercial Sales - Walmart

Location: Field – Bentonville, AR

Who We Are

For more than a century, L’Oréal has devoted its energy, innovation, and scientific excellence solely to one business: Beauty. Our goal is to offer each and every person around the world the best of beauty in terms of quality, efficacy, safety, sincerity and responsibility to satisfy all beauty needs and desires in their infinite diversity.

At L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty, our mission is to help everyone in their quest for healthy and beautiful skin. Our division is the world leader in dermo-cosmetics by adding health to beauty. Our brands portfolio includes CeraVe, La Roche-Posay, Vichy, SkinCeuticals and Skinbetter Science offering a range of skincare and haircare products to respond to all expectations linked to beauty and health of the skin.

What You Will Learn

As a strategic thinker with a passion for the beauty industry and a desire to drive category growth, you will master the development and execution of our skincare category strategy across Walmart’s rapidly evolving omni-channel ecosystem. This role will empower you to leverage advanced shopper understanding, Walmart Data Ventures/Scintilla analysis, and omni-channel expertise to accelerate the growth of our powerhouse derm portfolio. You will operate as a collaborative team member with a deep understanding of the retail landscape, gaining invaluable experience in identifying and capitalizing on emerging digital, AI, and rapid-delivery trends.

Position Overview

As the Customer Development Manager for Walmart within L'Oréal Dermatological Beauty (LDB), you will serve as both the commercial account strategist and the advanced data catalyst driving our business within Walmart’s rapidly evolving digital and physical ecosystem. You will leverage Walmart Scintilla, Data Ventures platform, and Retail Link to unlock omnichannel, insights, translating first-party data into future-forward growth strategies for our powerhouse derm brands (CeraVe, La Roche-Posay).

Strategic Account Management

Business Intelligence & Omnichannel Leadership

Act as the internal power user for Walmart Data Ventures Scintilla platform, extracting granular first-party omnichannel data (basket affinity, loyalty, lifetime value) to shape commercial strategy.Create the online vision for LDB brands, aligning with Walmart's rapidly evolving ecosystem (Omnichannel/Digital, AI Optimization, and Rapid Delivery).Collaborate with e-retail and consumer experience teams to execute plans and create a seamless Online-Plus-Offline (O+O) experience.

Reporting & Operational Execution

Deliver comprehensive commentary to supplement weekly performance reporting, tracking key business drivers, shipments, retail sales, and events.Lead end-to-end Line Review Preparation, partnering with cross-functional teams to build data-backed sales presentations and strategic proposals.Drive Category Insights & Analysis: Serve as the resident expert on category analysis for your brands, competitive brands, and the overall skincare/emerging categories. Develop opportunities from top-door analysis, new item/hero item evaluation, and weekly inventory reviews.Manage Item Set Up & Maintenance, ensuring flawless execution of data integrity across retail systems.Coordinate Mod Room execution and Sample management, ensuring physical and digital presentations meet retailer standards.Oversee planning and execution for retail Displays.

Main Interfaces

Commercial VP / Account Directors / Business AnalystInternal Sales Support Teams (Trade, Analytics, Customer Marketing, Category Development, Finance, Supply Chain, etc.)Assigned retailer touchpoints across various business units within Walmart.

Measures of Success

Commercial & Category Growth: Successful delivery of sales targets, distribution points, ROI, and profitable growth across core skincare and emerging categories (e.g., First Aid, Baby).Data Ventures & Omnichannel Mastery: Effective utilization and translation of Walmart Data Ventures and Scintilla platforms into winning Joint Business Planning (JBP) strategies, driving e-share expansion, digital shelf optimization, and rapid-delivery metrics.Strategic Partnership & Alignment: Positive retailer scorecards and strong collaborative relationships with internal stakeholders and Walmart buying teams.Operational & Execution Rigor: Effective weekly reporting commentary, timely item set-up & maintenance, display planning, and mod room/line review preparation.Team & Collaborative Impact: Active cross-functional leadership, ongoing support and development of junior team members, and positive Team 360° feedback.

What We Are Looking For

A results-oriented individual who can translate market and shopper insights into actionable strategies, contributing to profitable growth for the LDB Walmart business. You will possess a solid understanding of commercial principles, strong analytical skills, and the ability to effectively communicate with internal and external stakeholders.

Experience: 4–5+ years of relevant commercial, sales, or advanced analytical experience in CPG, with direct experience managing the Walmart account.Technical Expertise: Proven mastery of Walmart Data Ventures, Scintilla, and Retail Link (DSS/IDW). Experience with syndicated data (Circana/IRI) is a strong plus.Skills: Proficient in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel & PowerPoint. Strong analytical skills with the ability to collect, organize, and interpret large sets of retail data into compelling business narratives.Ecosystem Acumen: Deep knowledge of retailer strategies, digital shelf dynamics, omnichannel retail levers, and competitor landscapes.Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Economics, Supply Chain, or a related field.

Access to Company Perks (VIP Access to L’Oréal’s Internal Shop for Discounted Products, Monthly Mobile Allowance) Learning & Development Opportunities for Career Progression (Unlimited Access to E-learnings, Lunch & Learn Sessions, Mentorship Programs, & More!)   Employee Resource Groups (Think Tanks and Innovation Squads)   Access to Mental Health & Wellness Programs    

Authorization to work in the United States on a full-time, permanent, ongoing basis is required. No immigration support/sponsorship offered for this role

The Social Intelligence capability has been built to support stakeholders across Brand Marketing, Consumer & Marketplace Insights, Social Strategy & Community, Foresight, Innovation, Category Strategy, Corporate Communication and other teams; ultimately, our goal is to fully embed the capability throughout Nestle USA and empower stakeholders across every department to act upon real-time social media insights.

The role will work in collaboration with other stakeholders within the Center of Demand Generation, including but not limited to Foresight, Consumer Insights, Digital Analytics, Marketing Analytics, Digital Shelf & eCommerce, Shopper Insights and Innovation, to provide capabilities and services that consistently identify, generate & distribute actionable & timely insights to Nestle USA’s 25+ Brand Marketing teams.

The Senior Analyst will be expected to work with our stakeholder teams to understand Nestle USA’s business objectives and brand strategies across a wide variety of product categories such as coffee, coffee creamer, chocolate & desserts, frozen meals, pizza, snacking, baking ingredients, noodles and sauces. Day-to-day activities vary given the nature of our business, but the Senior Analyst can expect to balance answering business questions through in-depth analysis using multiple technologies, collaborating with stakeholders in key meetings, developing and executing self-service training programs, identifying & helping implement new technology features, working with vendors and attending leadership presentations.

On top of the various product categories we support and the multiple technologies we use, the world of social media and AI-driven technology changes rapidly. Social Listening, LLM Listening & Related Social Media Research, including Presentation to Stakeholders. Leverage Nestle USA’s Digital & Social Intelligence technology stack to conduct in-depth research about our brands, competitors, product categories and relevant cultural trends, using the insights to deliver a persuasive & visual story to stakeholders that drives action within their key initiatives. This includes navigating technology that handles every facet of Digital & Social Intelligence, such as social listening, ratings & reviews listening, LLM Listening / GEO / AEO, emerging trend identification, social audience persona building, influencer evaluation and owned content performance benchmarking. Stakeholder Training & Guidance. Assist the Digital & Social Intelligence Manager in managing an analysis request queue, which assigns priority to each ad-hoc social research request based on impact to the business, level of effort and urgency. This includes keeping track of stakeholder check-in cadences to ensure the Digital & Social Intelligence team is consistently engaging each key stakeholder group. Tool Output Scanning & Insights Identification. Review the automated reporting outputs from the various tools, including weekly/bi-weekly/monthly AI-driven reports and real-time email alerts, to ensure continuous improvement in the quality of the automated outputs while also mining for actionable insights that need to be flagged to our stakeholders for further discussion & potential action.Tool Maintenance & Governance. Assist in the day-to-day management of the tools, from user access to dashboard/report quality, flagging issues or needs to the Digital & Social Intelligence Manager while collaborating with 3rd party and shared service support teams. Vendor Collaboration. Partnering with analysts from 3rd parties and shared service teams on key research projects and key feature advancements, as well as brainstorming and providing feedback to tool providers on ideal features and functionality that maximize actionability.

DESIRED EXPERIENCE:

rows.descriptionText:
Director, Analytical Stability & Innovation, Research & Innovation - Clark, New Jersey

Life is too short for a boring career, so build an extraordinary one with us. We believe your career should spark the same thrill and curiosity as your personal interests. Creativity drives everything we do, turning ideas into meaningful impact. With opportunities across brands, markets, and divisions, your growth knows no boundaries.

Who We Are

Join us at L’Oréal, the world's #1 beauty company present in over 150 markets. For over a century, we have been transforming; fueled by data, tech, innovation, and science. Together, we tackle big challenges while making sure we stay committed to making the world a more inclusive and a better place for everyone & our planet.

At L’Oréal Research & Innovation we are pushing the boundaries of Science & Tech. We invest heavily in cutting-edge research, leveraging advanced technologies to understand skin, hair, and microbiome, while discovering new active ingredients and launching outperforming formulas. Our 3,500 L'Oréal R&I experts leverage Science & Technology to invent safe, trustable, sustainable & responsible beauty products and experiences that will change people’s lives.

We are seeking a Director to join our Analytical Chemistry team in our state-of-the-art Clark, New Jersey research facility, leading our end-to-end R&I stability programs and managing the Analytical Innovation & Expertise team. In this role, you will provide strategic operational and scientific leadership to ensure robust stability, regulatory compliance, and data-driven insights for our OTC and beauty care portfolios, while continuing to champion analytical capability building and innovation. You will be responsible for the management, development, and technical upskilling of the team.

A Day In The Life

Lead End-to-End Stability Programs: Create, review, approve, and oversee comprehensive stability study protocols and timelines (covering OTC and cosmetics) including sample collection, storage conditions, and analytical testing to support product development and go-to-market initiatives.Drive Digital & Predictive Analytical Transformation: Shape the strategy for predictive chemical stability using advanced modeling, data visualization, statistical tools, and kinetic modeling to forecast shelf-life and degradation pathways across the product lifecycle. Regulatory & Audit SME: Serve as the primary subject matter expert for analytical methodologies, stability programs, and compliance during internal and external audits. Ensure strict adherence to FDA, Health Canada, GMP, GLP, and ICH guidelines.Team Leadership & Upskilling: Manage the daily functional work of the analytical Innovation & Expertise team (7 direct reports with diverse expertise, including trace and surface science), mentoring and upskilling the team in new digital and analytical techniques.Cross-Functional & Métier Partnership: Partner closely with key métiers, process development, formulation, manufacturing, QA, and regulatory affairs teams to manage testing expectations, resolve project bottlenecks, and align analytical strategies with business priorities.Strategic Leadership: Be a creative and strategic leader with passion for innovation and show ability to build a forward-thinking outlook, remove barriers, develop people, and continuously thrive to raise the technical skills/expertise of the staff members.CRO Management: Oversee external contract research organizations and contract manufacturing partners regarding vendor selection, qualification, and analytical contracting.Capability Development: Guide assay, trace, impurity, and degradation product analysis, ensuring robust method development, validation, and transfer (internally and externally), ensuring compliance with relevant ICH, GMPs, and regulatory guidelines.

We Are Looking For: You’re a great match for this role if you are an operational leader, integrator, and problem-solver with deep expertise in stability programs, regulatory compliance, and laboratory capability building.

Education: A PhD in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related scientific/engineering discipline is required.Experience: 7+ years of relevant industry experience in analytical chemistry supporting OTC and/or stability programs.Strong, demonstrated experience managing end-to-end stability programs from product development to launch in a GMP/OTC environment is a must.Strong knowledge and practical experience in statistics, predictive analytics/modeling (e.g., chemometrics, stability kinetics/Arrhenius Law), and data visualization.Strong regulatory knowledge of FDA, Health Canada, ICH guidelines, and compendial standards pertaining to OTC products, quality systems, and method validation.Experience overseeing and working with contract research organizations (CROs) and external vendors.Strong experience managing direct reports in a laboratory setting, with a track record of innovation, capability building, and upskilling technical teams.Strong experimental background in chromatography (LC/GC), mass spectrometry and LC/GC-MS-based systems (QTrap LC-MS/MS, TripleTOF LC-MS/MS, etc.) to guide expert teams effectively.Excellent cross-functional communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to manage expectations across diverse business métiers.Highly effective organizational planning, project management, and problem-solving skills.The ability to be onsite, in the office/laboratory at least 5 days a week, as this is an essential function of the position (required).Authorization to work in the United States is required. No sponsorship is offered for this role. (required).The ability to lift 25 lbs (11.3 kg) (required).

What’s In It For You

A place for you to leave your comfort zone and grow beyond your potential (here, you’ll be encouraged to try new things and take risks!)Real responsibility from day 1, there’s no sitting on the sidelines at L’OréalAn environment where people of every ethnicity, social background, age, religion, gender and sexual orientation as well as people with disabilities are accepted, can speak up, will thrive and are celebrated!A place where you can contribute to something bigger! rows.title: Digital & Social Intelligence Senior Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Foods you love. Brands you trust. And a career that empowers you to grow.

At Nestlé USA, we’re all working towards the same goal – to delight and deliver for our consumers. With a rich portfolio of beloved brands, including DiGiorno, Toll House, and Coffee mate, in 97% of U.S. households, we have a unique opportunity – and responsibility – to be there for every moment in our consumers’ lives.

Joining Nestlé means becoming part of an inclusive workplace that inspires innovation, encourages strategic thinking and creativity, and celebrates your achievements. No matter where you work within the organization, you are empowered to challenge the status quo, embrace risk-taking, and pioneer new ideas. Our supportive and collaborative environment encourages bold ambitions and continuous learning so that everyone can grow and thrive.

This position is not eligible for Visa Sponsorship.

Reporting into the Digital & Social Intelligence Manager within the Commercial Excellence organization, the Digital & Social Intelligence Senior Analyst will be a crucial addition to a team whose mission is to implement an adaptive, industry-leading Social Intelligence capability into Nestle USA that is considered a trusted source of actionable, real-time insight into consumer perception & culture. The Social Intelligence capability has been built to support stakeholders across Brand Marketing, Consumer & Marketplace Insights, Social Strategy & Community, Foresight, Innovation, Category Strategy, Corporate Communication and other teams; ultimately, our goal is to fully embed the capability throughout Nestle USA and empower stakeholders across every department to act upon real-time social media insights.

Additionally, the Senior Analyst will be a crucial member of the emerging cross-functional capability of AI Readiness by supporting LLM Listening & Visibility analysis, including tool implementation & governance, stakeholder support and incorporation into Social Intelligence analysis deliverables.

After supporting the final stages of the Social Intelligence capability’s implementation across Nestle USA, and the incorporation of LLM Listening into our processes, the Digital & Social Intelligence Senior Analyst’s role will focus on robust stakeholder relationship building with teams across the organization, working hand-in-hand with stakeholders to provide consistent, timely & actionable insights for our brands, while forging a continuous stakeholder feedback loop on our offerings. The insights the Analyst will deliver will originate from both cadenced and ad-hoc research requests, while the feedback the Senior Analyst gathers will inform how we optimize & evolve the Digital & Social Intelligence capability over time using ever-evolving AI-driven technology.

The Senior Analyst will be expected to balance supporting stakeholders by fulfilling research requests using our best-in-class technology stack, while also training the stakeholders to be able to leverage the technology to find insights on their own. This balance will allow the Senior Analyst, along with the rest of the Digital & Social Intelligence team, to focus our efforts on the most important in-depth analysis the organization needs, while empowering our stakeholders to conduct their own light monitoring of day-to-day digital & social insights questions. The role will work in collaboration with other stakeholders within the Center of Demand Generation, including but not limited to Foresight, Consumer Insights, Digital Analytics, Marketing Analytics, Digital Shelf & eCommerce, Shopper Insights and Innovation, to provide capabilities and services that consistently identify, generate & distribute actionable & timely insights to Nestle USA’s 25+ Brand Marketing teams.

The Senior Analyst will be expected to work with our stakeholder teams to understand Nestle USA’s business objectives and brand strategies across a wide variety of product categories such as coffee, coffee creamer, chocolate & desserts, frozen meals, pizza, snacking, baking ingredients, noodles and sauces. Day-to-day activities vary given the nature of our business, but the Senior Analyst can expect to balance answering business questions through in-depth analysis using multiple technologies, collaborating with stakeholders in key meetings, developing and executing self-service training programs, identifying & helping implement new technology features, working with vendors and attending leadership presentations.

On top of the various product categories we support and the multiple technologies we use, the world of social media and AI-driven technology changes rapidly. Therefore, a balance of technical skill, strategic thinking, proactivity, flexibility and a solution-seeking attitude is crucial for success in this role.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Social Listening, LLM Listening & Related Social Media Research, including Presentation to Stakeholders. Leverage Nestle USA’s Digital & Social Intelligence technology stack to conduct in-depth research about our brands, competitors, product categories and relevant cultural trends, using the insights to deliver a persuasive & visual story to stakeholders that drives action within their key initiatives. This includes navigating technology that handles every facet of Digital & Social Intelligence, such as social listening, ratings & reviews listening, LLM Listening / GEO / AEO, emerging trend identification, social audience persona building, influencer evaluation and owned content performance benchmarking. Where applicable, this also includes combining findings with other data sources outside of Social Intelligence, often via collaboration with our broader Digital Analytics, Marketing Analytics and Consumer Insights teams, to provide comprehensive analysis to the stakeholder. Stakeholder Training & Guidance. Assist in the development and execution of training programs, including building training material, leading office hours and sitting one-on-one with stakeholders to guide them through use cases for social listening & social intelligence that build confidence in their ability to navigate the technology to find insights.Stakeholder Request Management. Assist the Digital & Social Intelligence Manager in managing an analysis request queue, which assigns priority to each ad-hoc social research request based on impact to the business, level of effort and urgency. This includes keeping track of stakeholder check-in cadences to ensure the Digital & Social Intelligence team is consistently engaging each key stakeholder group. Tool Output Scanning & Insights Identification. Review the automated reporting outputs from the various tools, including weekly/bi-weekly/monthly AI-driven reports and real-time email alerts, to ensure continuous improvement in the quality of the automated outputs while also mining for actionable insights that need to be flagged to our stakeholders for further discussion & potential action.Tool Maintenance & Governance. Assist in the day-to-day management of the tools, from user access to dashboard/report quality, flagging issues or needs to the Digital & Social Intelligence Manager while collaborating with 3rd party and shared service support teams. Vendor Collaboration. Partnering with analysts from 3rd parties and shared service teams on key research projects and key feature advancements, as well as brainstorming and providing feedback to tool providers on ideal features and functionality that maximize actionability. 
REQUIREMENTS AND MINIMUM EDUCATION LEVEL:

Bachelor's degree in marketing, market research, analytics, communications, business, economics, or related field3-5 years of experience in social listening and additional social research, including in-tool navigational experience and strategic storytelling of analysis results.3-5 years in a strategic role working with data analytics, with a focus on developing strong dashboards and/or other automatically refreshable visualizations that empower stakeholders to quickly identify key takeaways from data
DESIRED EXPERIENCE:

Experience using Talkwalker, Nichefire, Yogi, Audiense, Creator IQ, Sprinklr or similar tools throughout every part of the process: query building, dashboard visualization, automated report building and ultimately in-depth analysis of key takeawaysFamiliarity with the emerging LLM Listening & Visibility / GEO / AEO analysis space, including tools such as ProfoundStrong understanding of how AI can be used to support Digital & Social Intelligence workstreams, including prompt-writing best practices to focus the observation summarizations of AI assistantsStrong research experience and familiarity with the process for developing consumer, category & cultural insightsStrong storytelling experience through the creation and presentation of compelling slide decksAbility to translate business needs into strategic social intelligence frameworks that can be executed & replicated across a large organizationFamiliarity with foresight use cases, identifying and analyzing trend signals from social media that ladder up to larger cultural movements or consumer behavior shiftsUnderstanding of the social media landscape, dynamics of community interaction, social best practices, and digital analytics toolsStrong communication and interpersonal skillsAbility to execute multiple projects at once across various stakeholder teams throughout a large organization
ADDITIONAL PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:

Familiarity with experimentation and A/B testing of social/digital content executionsFamiliarity with Google Analytics and Google Tag Manager for website analyticsFamiliarity with Salesforce Marketing Cloud and its analytics functionalitiesFamiliarity with Power BI to create and visualize data from disparate data sets 
Salary: $100,000.00 to $120,000.00 per year

Bonus Eligibility: Yes

The pay range provided is a good faith estimate for the position at the time of posting. Final compensation may vary based on factors including but not limited to knowledge, skills and abilities as well as geographic location. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at top of range.

Nestlé offers performance-based incentives and a competitive total rewards package, which includes a 401k with company match, healthcare coverage and a broad range of other benefits. Incentives and/or benefit packages may vary depending on the position. Learn more at https://www.nestlejobs.com/nestle-in-the-us-benefits

The Brand PR Director for Mars Snacking North America helps lead the earned-first strategy and execution of brand communications for Mars Snacking North America’s portfolio of iconic, billion-dollar confectionary brands including M&M’S®, SNICKERS®, SKITTLES®, and EXTRA®. to elevate the brands’ presence, reputation, consumer engagement and cultural relevance.

This role oversees the development and execution of breakthrough earned media programs that generate talkability, strengthen brand equity, and fuel long term business growth. What are we looking for?

Bachelor’s degree in communications, marketing, journalism or associated profession is required, or the equivalent combination of education, training and experience.10+ years of strong communications and leadership capabilities for consumer-facing brands, with a proven track record of delivering earned-first, integrated communications strategies that outperform KPIs.Understanding of and experience in developing reputation-driving strategies and programs tied to consumer brands.Expertise in brand communications and navigating the consumer media and social landscape.Experience with strategic agency management, including scoping, contracting, and success measurement.Proven success in leading communications across multiple brands and portfolio is preferred.Influencing without direct authority to motivate teams and challenge “status quo” at all levels within the business to achieve shared objectives.Knowledge of Retail, Paid Media, Influencer, Social, and CP channel management is critical for cross functional project management.Digital-first mindset and understanding of the consumer media landscape.Line management experience to help lead through sometimes-ambiguous setting, with the ability to adapt quickly. Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by the Five Principles.

Join a purpose driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.

rows.title: Data Insight Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Because we strive to put people first.

Culture, our way.

Technology at Primark

What’s a career at Primark all about? The positive impact you’re making, the experiences you’re having and the people you’re with. You’re our inspiration. Embrace what sets you apart, own your career and develop in ways you never expected. Leave your mark. And do it your way.

Our technology team is actively seeking an Insight Analyst to join its Applied Insights & Analytics team, helping transform data into actionable insights that drive better business decisions and commercial value. Working across areas including Trading, Buying & Merchandising, Supply Chain, Retail Operations, Finance, and Customer teams, the role involves analysing data, identifying opportunities, answering key business questions, and delivering clear, data-driven recommendations. As part of Primark’s innovative technology function, the successful candidate will collaborate with stakeholders and technology teams to support business growth, leveraging strong analytical skills and commercial awareness to turn complex data into meaningful outcomes.

What You’ll Get

This role is a hybrid opportunity, offering 2-3 days Working from office.

People are at the heart of what we do here, so it’s essential we provide you with the right environment to perform at your very best.

Let’s talk lifestyle: Healthcare, pension, and potential bonus. 27 days of leave, plus bank holidays and if you want, you can buy 5 more. Because Primark is all about tailoring to you, we offer Tax Saver Tickets, fitness centre, and a subsidised cafeteria.

What You’ll Do as Insight Analyst

In your role, you’ll collaborate with different people across a range of skillsets. Here’s a flavour of your day-to-day:

Deliver impactful business insights by partnering with stakeholders to understand commercial challenges, frame key business questions, and translate data into actionable recommendations that drive better decision-making.Analyse and interpret complex datasets using SQL, insight applications, and reporting tools to uncover trends, identify risks and opportunities, and support decisions across Trading, Customer, Retail Operations, and other commercial functions.Create compelling data-driven stories by turning complex analytical outputs into clear, concise insights, visualisations, and recommendations that are easily understood by both technical and non-technical audiences.Develop and enhance reporting solutions, including dashboards, scorecards, and management reporting packs, ensuring outputs are accurate, consistent, user-friendly, and focused on delivering measurable business value.Drive continuous improvement by identifying manual processes, recurring business questions, and opportunities to streamline, standardise, and optimise reporting and insight delivery across the organisation.Collaborate with cross-functional Data & Analytics teams, including Business Partners, Senior Analysts, Data Engineers, and Data Scientists, while maintaining strong data quality standards and ensuring trusted, insight-led outcomes that support commercial growth and operational performance.

What You’ll Bring

Here at Primark, we want everyone to feel valued – so please bring your authentic self to work, of course with some other key experience and abilities for this role in particular:

Experience in analytics, insights, reporting, or commercial analysis within retail, apparel, grocery, FMCG, or other fast-paced consumer-focused environments, with strong SQL skills and the ability to confidently query, analyse, and interpret data to support business decisions.Proficiency in Power BI, Tableau, or similar reporting and analytics tools, with experience creating insightful dashboards, scorecards, KPI frameworks, and performance reporting that drive measurable business outcomes.Strong commercial acumen with the ability to connect data and analysis to sales growth, conversion, margin improvement, markdown optimisation, stock availability, customer performance, and operational effectiveness.Excellent communication and data storytelling skills, with the ability to transform complex analytical findings into clear, compelling narratives, visualisations, recommendations, and decision-support materials for a wide range of stakeholders.Proven stakeholder management and commercial partnering experience, working collaboratively to understand business priorities, challenge assumptions constructively, shape analytical requirements, and deliver actionable insights linked to tangible value and benefits realisation.A proactive and solution-focused mindset, comfortable working with imperfect data, applying appropriate quality checks, improving reporting processes, simplifying decision-making, and identifying opportunities to enhance productivity, reporting efficiency, and overall business performance.

Does this sound like you? Great, because we can’t wait to see what you’ll bring. You’ll be supported within a team of equally capable people, celebrating who you are and aiding you reach your potential. At Primark, we’re excited about our future - and we’re excited to develop yours.

About Primark

At Primark, people matter. They’re the beating heart of our business and the reason we’ve grown from our first store in Dublin in 1969 to over 80,000 colleagues and over 480 stores in 18 countries today and growing.

So, what’s a career at Primark all about? The positive impact you’re making, the experiences you’re having and the people you’re with. It’s that feeling that turns a job into something more. Celebrating the wins, working at pace, and pulling through the challenging times with passion, courage, and your team by your side. It’s what drives us every day.

You’re our driving force. Embrace what sets you apart, own your career and develop in ways you never expected. Leave your mark. And do it your way.

Merchandising at Primark

They’re the beating heart of our business and the reason we’ve grown from our first store in Dublin in 1969 to a £9bn+ turnover business a over 80,000 colleagues and over 440 stores in 17 countries today. Description & Requirements

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

At EA, we believe games are powerful because they bring together multiple ways people engage: play, watch, create, and connect. And increasingly, the biggest entertainment platforms aren't just places to consume content — they're places where communities build.

rows.title: Principal, Product Management - Loyalty Execution Platform
rows.descriptionText:
Overview

Company Description

We are seeking an experienced and strategic Product Manager to drive the evolution of our loyalty execution platform. This role sits at the intersection of product management, customer loyalty strategy, customer analytics, artificial intelligence, client engagement, and market intelligence. The ideal candidate will play a critical role in shaping our loyalty technology roadmap by gathering market insights, understanding client and prospect needs, and translating those inputs into innovative product capabilities that deliver measurable value.

This individual will identify emerging trends in customer loyalty and engagement. They will anticipate future market needs. They will help define how customer data and analytics improve the loyalty experience by building more personalized, relevant, and effective interactions. The successful candidate combines deep loyalty marketing expertise with a strong background in SaaS product development and execution. This position will also require a solid understanding of customer analytics and innovative use of first- and third-party data to create personalized experiences for consumers.

Candidates will ideally be located in the Dallas, Chicago, or Denver metropolitan areas. Boston and New York may also be considered locations.

Responsibilities

Product Strategy & Roadmap Development

Serve as a key contributor to the strategic direction and roadmap of the loyalty execution platform.Find opportunities for new features, functionality, and platform enhancements that improve client outcomes and drive business growth.Develop cases, product requirements, and implementation plans for new capabilities.Prioritize initiatives based on customer value, market demand, strategic fit, and business impact.

AI & Personalization Strategy

Help define and complete the company's vision for incorporating AI, customer strategy, and analytics throughout the loyalty experience.Find opportunities for technology-powered capabilities that enable clients to deliver more personalized customer journeys, communications, offers, rewards, and experiences using Epsilon’s proprietary customer data assets.Evaluate emerging AI technologies, tools, and market developments to determine their applicability within the loyalty platform.Partner with product, engineering, data, analytics, and customer teams to translate AI & personalization concepts into scalable product functionality.Develop use-cases and requirements for predictive, recommendation, segmentation, and personalization capabilities that create measurable client value.Find opportunities to integrate Epsilon’s differentiated data, activation, identity, and digital assets into the loyalty platform.

Market & Industry Intelligence

Stay current on trends, innovations, competitive offerings, and emerging technologies within the customer loyalty, customer engagement, AI, and marketing technology industries.Monitor industry developments and see opportunities to strengthen the platform's competitive position.Anticipate future client needs and evolving market requirements to inform long-term product strategy.

Customer & Prospect Insights

rows.title: Treasury Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Position Summary

We are seeking an analytical, detail-oriented Financial Analyst – Treasury & Cash Flow to support treasury operations, cash forecasting, liquidity analysis and financial reporting.

The role covers direct and indirect cash flow forecasting, monitoring actual cash performance against forecast, and explaining key variances and drivers to support treasury and business decisions.

The ideal candidate has a strong finance and accounting foundation, advanced Excel skills, and the ability to turn large financial datasets into clear, actionable insights.

Key Responsibilities

Treasury & Cash Management

Support day-to-day treasury activities and global cash management processes.Monitor cash balances, cash movements, liquidity and funding needs across entities.Analyze historical and projected cash movements to identify trends, risks, surplus cash and opportunities for efficient cash utilization.Support treasury reporting and periodic management reviews.


Cash Flow Forecasting

Prepare and maintain direct cash flow forecasts, including customer collections, vendor payments, payroll, taxes, capital expenditures, intercompany settlements, and other operating cash flows.Prepare and analyze indirect cash flow forecasts, reconciling operating performance to cash generation.Work closely with AR, AP, Payroll, FP&A, Accounting and other Finance teams to obtain and validate forecast inputs.Compare actual cash flows against forecast, explain material variances, and improve forecast accuracy through ongoing review of assumptions and historical trends.Support short- and medium-term liquidity forecasting and scenario analysis.


Required Skills & Qualifications

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Commerce, Business Administration or a related field.Approximately 4–6 years of relevant experience in Treasury, Cash Management, Financial Planning & Analysis, Accounting, Controllership or Corporate Finance.Strong understanding of liquidity management and both direct and indirect cash flow forecasting methodologies.Solid grounding in financial statements, working capital and accounting fundamentals, including accruals, prepayments, AR, AP and balance sheet movements.Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including PivotTables, XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP, SUMIFS, IF formulas, data analysis, reconciliation techniques and handling large datasets.Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with attention to detail.


Preferred Skills

Experience working in a multinational or global finance environment.Exposure to ERP and financial reporting systems (NetSuite, Oracle or similar), treasury management systems, banking platforms or cash management tools.Knowledge of Power BI, Power Query or other data visualization/automation tools is a plus.Experience working with multiple currencies and international entities is advantageous.
